When a list is renamed in Archie's store, your copy takes the new name, unless you renamed it yourself. A list whose columns you changed, but not its name, is still renamed.

entries.t: Unasked messages wait for the answer
entries.s: Messages your agent sends without being asked, like the morning list, a card about new mail or a routine's report, wait until it has finished answering you.
entries.x: In your chat with your agent. A message written once waits five minutes at most, then goes. Reminders you set and replies you scheduled are not held. They go at the minute you asked for. It waits only for an answer in the same chat. It still arrives unasked, and a reminder can land in the middle of an answer.

entries.s: When your agent sends something without being asked, a line over it says so and what it is, like "Sent on its own at 6:30 AM: your morning list."
entries.x: Over the message, in your own chat with your agent. On an iPhone, Archie Mobile shows the same line. A routine is named by its name, and a reminder as "a reminder you set". A card from the mail or text watch says only "Sent on its own". Your own chat in Archie and Archie Mobile only. A chat app has no such line, and a teammate's chat is not marked.

entries.t: Links Archie never read are cut back
entries.s: If a reply holds a web link to a site Archie never read or found in a search, the link is cut back to the site's front page.
entries.x: In your agent's replies. It checks the site only. A link deep in a site that came up in a search or a page it read stays whole, even if that page was never opened. It does not check that the site exists, so a link can still fail to open. When unsure it leaves a link alone, so a short site name mentioned elsewhere keeps its whole link.

entries.s: Type /pending and everything still waiting on you is posted again at the bottom of the chat. The earlier copy says the newest card replaced it, and its buttons go.
entries.x: Type /pending in your chat with your agent. Type /pending and send it. Not on Signal or iMessage, which cannot change a message once it is sent. There the old copy stays, and a press on it is answered once. Every copy of a draft is the same draft, so one already sent answers "Already handled."

entries.t: Suggested asks in an empty chat
entries.s: An empty chat suggests up to three things you can ask your agent right now, picked from the skills it has and the accounts you connected. Tap one and it goes as if you had typed it.
entries.x: In your chat with your agent, while the chat is empty. Tap one of the suggestions in the empty chat. On a chat app, the welcome after you claim your agent lists the same asks for you to type. Archie Mobile does not show them yet. On a Mac only. Archie on Windows is still on 0.3.11, without it. The suggestions are fixed words, one for each skill and line of work, picked by what is installed and connected. An agent with nothing ready shows the empty chat as before. No suggestion asks you to connect or install anything.

entries.t: Say a message instead of typing
entries.s: Press the microphone beside the message box to speak a message; Archie turns it into words on your computer, and only the words go to your AI company.
entries.x: In the chat, the microphone beside the message box, shown while the box is empty and the agent is running. Press the microphone and speak. Press Done. Choose Put it in the box to edit the words first, or Send as a voice note. Archie Mobile's talk button records a voice note and sends it, locked, to your computer, which turns it into words. It needs a one-time download of about 195 MB, and Archie names the size before it starts. English only. A voice note keeps its recording in your agent's folder so you can play it back. Put it in the box keeps nothing. A person has used it on a Mac and never yet on Windows.

entries.t: Spoken replies on iMessage come as audio messages
entries.s: On iMessage, when your agent answers out loud, the answer comes as an audio message in the Messages thread, instead of a file to open somewhere else.
entries.x: In Messages, in your conversation with your agent on iMessage. Send your agent a voice message on iMessage, or ask it to read something out. To choose when it answers out loud, open your agent's Personality tab and pick When you speak to it, Every time, or Never. Send the voice message from Messages on your iPhone, and the answer comes back in the same thread. iMessage needs a Mac, so this is on a Mac only. Its voices are a one-time download to the computer running Archie. Until they are there, it answers in writing. An answer to a voice message that would take more than about two minutes to say comes in writing, with a line saying why, unless you asked for it out loud. A typed message gets a written answer, unless the setting is Every time or you ask. Nobody has played one on a real iPhone yet.

entries.s: Archie Mobile, for iPhone and Android, reaches the agent on your computer, which locks every message with a key that only your phone also holds.
entries.x: On an agent's Setup tab, under Chat app, the Archie Mobile row has the link to get it and the code that connects it. Install Archie Mobile from the App Store on iPhone, or from the Android download. In Archie, open an agent's Setup tab and choose Chat app. On the Archie Mobile row, press Show the code. In Archie Mobile, press Scan and point the camera at the code. Setting up a new agent, press Continue with Archie Mobile once the code is on screen. You don't need a chat app as well. On iPhone from the App Store, and on Android as a download from a file rather than a store; the Android version is older, so newer features reach iPhone first. Your agent runs on your computer, so it has to be on, awake and running Archie for the phone to reach it. It does most of what you do at the computer. Signing in to an account still happens at the computer. We hold the locked messages and cannot read them. We can see when one was left, which Archie version wrote it, and whether a command is done. Whoever holds the phone holds the key. Disconnect every phone, under the code in Archie, cuts a lost phone off.

entries.t: Your agent on iMessage, with its own Apple ID
entries.s: On a Mac, your agent answers in iMessage in the chat you have with yourself, with its name on its replies, or on an Apple ID of its own.
entries.x: On the agent's Setup tab, under Chat app, iMessage, in Which Apple ID Messages uses for your agent. Make an Apple ID for your agent and sign a spare Mac's Messages into it. In Archie on that Mac, open the agent's Setup tab and choose Chat app, then iMessage. Under Which Apple ID Messages uses for your agent, pick the agent's own. Type the phone number or Apple ID email you will text it from. You text it from your iPhone's Messages like any other contact. The second way takes that Mac's Messages off your own Apple ID, so use a spare Mac. In the chat with yourself, Messages still shows each message twice. The name only makes your agent's half easy to read. Text Replies then reads the messages on the agent's Apple ID. Nobody has tried it yet on a real Mac signed into a second Apple ID.

entries.s: Turn on notifications in Archie Mobile and your phone shows reminders, reports, new mail, and replies to what you sent from it, even with the app closed.
entries.x: In Archie Mobile, under Settings, Notifications. In Archie Mobile, open Settings. Under Notifications, turn them on, and allow them when your phone asks. On iPhone, from Archie Mobile 1.3 with Archie 0.3.9 on the computer; the Android download does not have it yet. Your computer sends them, so it has to be on, awake and running Archie. Its window can be closed. Only the owner's phone gets them. A teammate's phone does not. On an agent with a chat app connected, a reply's notification comes about 15 seconds after your agent goes quiet. What each one says is locked on your computer and opened on your phone, so we, Apple and Google pass it along without reading it.

entries.t: A phone message waits for a sleeping computer
entries.s: A message sent from Archie Mobile while your computer sleeps waits and says so, and your agent answers it when the computer wakes, knowing it was sent earlier.
entries.x: In Archie Mobile, on the waiting message. To take back a waiting message, press Remove it. In Archie Mobile on iPhone and Android. Your agent answers only once the computer running Archie is on and Archie is open. Remove it works only if the computer has not picked the message up yet. Nobody has yet tried it on a real phone against a sleeping computer.

entries.t: Run a routine or tune a skill from your phone
entries.s: From Archie Mobile you can run a routine now, pick a skill's Response quality, and switch a skill's scheduled messages off and on.
entries.x: In Archie Mobile, on a skill's or routine's row, which opens in place. In Archie Mobile, open your agent's skills or routines. Press a row to open it, then press Run now or change a setting. In Archie Mobile on iPhone and Android. The computer running Archie does the work, so it has to be on, awake and running Archie. Connecting an account for a skill still happens at the computer. Nobody has watched it on a real phone yet.

entries.t: More of your agent's setup from your phone
entries.s: From Archie Mobile you can let in or block someone who messaged your agent, turn on calls to businesses, and paste your AI account's key. You can also change what Email Manager and Text Replies watch for, and say whose each mail account is.
entries.x: In Archie Mobile on an iPhone, under More and on the Skills tab. To let someone in or block them, open More, then Teammates, and press Let them in, Not now, or Block. To turn on calls, open More, then What it can do, then Call businesses. To paste your AI account's key, open More, then Response quality, and use AI account at the top. To change what Email Manager or Text Replies watches for, open it on the Skills tab. To say whose a mail account is, open More, then Connections, and pick under Whose is this? On an iPhone, from Archie Mobile 1.5. The Android download does not have it. On a Mac only. Archie on Windows is still on 0.3.11, without it. Letting people in and blocking them from the phone works on Archie for Teams only. Signing in to Google, Microsoft or Zoom, and Reconnect, stay at the computer. The phone shows which account stopped opening and where to press Reconnect. Watch my texts, the Mac's permission to read Messages, and Another provider are set up at the computer. A key you paste is checked with that company before it is kept. It travels to your computer through our phone mailbox, locked so we can't open it. The rest of the Email Manager and Text Replies settings stay on the computer, and the phone says where. The computer running Archie does each of these, so it has to be awake, connected to the internet, and running Archie. Nobody has tried it on a real phone yet.

entries.s: Text your agent from your phone and it answers in the first line and keeps the reply short, with no headings.
entries.x: Messages you type in Archie Mobile or a chat app, and on a teammate's phone. It works for messages from Archie Mobile, a teammate's phone, or a chat app. It is what your agent is told. Nothing cuts a reply short. Typed messages only. A press, a routine or a watch is answered as before, and so is a message typed at the computer. A chat app counts as a phone, because Archie cannot tell where it is being read.

entries.t: When your chat app stops reaching your agent
entries.s: If messages on your chat app stop reaching your agent for more than half an hour, Archie tells you in Archie, and so on Archie Mobile, with what to do on the computer. It says so again once they get through.
entries.x: In your conversation with your agent in Archie, and on Archie Mobile. Never on the chat app itself, since that is what stopped. Archie Mobile shows it in your conversation, and on iPhone, from 1.3, as a notification when its notifications are on. On a Mac only. Archie on Windows is still on 0.3.11, without it. It waits half an hour, so a closed lid or a short outage passes without a word, and it says so once. The computer running Archie has to be on, awake and running Archie, because that computer is the one that notices. That the chat app may need connecting again is its best guess. The one cause it names for certain is two things using the same Telegram bot. The fix happens at the computer: in Archie, on the agent's Setup tab, under Chat app, connect it again. Nobody has seen it on a real phone yet.

entries.t: Email goes out when you send it or set a time
entries.s: Your agent drafts email replies and can't send one on its own. Each draft comes to your chat as a card with Send on it, and nothing leaves your account until you send it or set a time for it.
entries.x: On an email draft card in your chat: Send, Edit it, Send later and Dismiss. Read the draft on its card. Press Send, or Send later and pick a time. Press Edit it to change it first, or Dismiss. On a chat app with no buttons, reply send. The card and its buttons reach Archie Mobile and chat apps with buttons. Where there are no buttons, reply send. A reply set for a time goes out then with nobody pressing anything, and calls itself off if they write back first. Only your press sets a time. Your agent can suggest one on the card, and you press it. Each Send sends the one reply on its card. A draft with a blank still in it won't send until you fill it in. Gmail and Outlook stay read-only unless you check Let it send replies when you connect them. Every send is recorded on the Jobs tab, with when Send was pressed and who pressed it.

entries.t: Edit a draft in a pop-up
entries.s: Press Edit it on an email or text draft and a pop-up shows the message it answers. It has three ways to change the draft: type it your way, tell your agent what to change, or have it write three more.
entries.x: On an email or text draft card, press Edit it. The pop-up has Use my words, Rewrite it for me, and Other versions. Press Edit it on the draft. Pick Use my words to type it yourself, Rewrite it for me to say what should change, or Other versions for three more. In Rewrite it for me, you can point at something your agent can look up, like an earlier email or your calendar, and it looks before it rewrites. Press Save, Rewrite it, or Write three. In Use my words, Clear empties the box to start over. On an iPhone, from Archie Mobile 1.3, Edit it opens the same pop-up. The Android download shows the three choices on the card. Saving changes the draft and sends nothing. Send on the card is still what sends it. If your agent can't find what you pointed at, it says so and leaves it out. It looks only where it can, with what you connected. Looking something up for a rewrite has not been tried on a real mailbox yet. The email it answers is read from your mailbox when the pop-up opens, and none of it is kept. If the mailbox can't be reached, the pop-up shows the card's one-line summary and says why. The cursor starts at the end of the letter, above your name. When some of your words sit under your name, Move them above it moves them up, and nothing moves on its own. Rewrite it for me doesn't use Write like me. On Telegram, Discord, Slack, Signal and iMessage, Edit it shows the three choices on the card, and a change you type comes back as a new card.

entries.t: Drafts waiting for you to press Send
entries.s: Every draft card says "Not sent yet." while it waits. Over the message box, a line such as "2 waiting to send" counts the drafts in this conversation, and pressing it opens the list.
entries.x: On each draft card, and over the message box in your chat with your agent. Press the line over the message box that says how many are waiting to send. In the list, press Send to send one, or Show to go to its card. On an iPhone, Archie Mobile shows the same line from 1.3, and the list and the grayed words from 1.4. It counts the drafts in the conversation on screen. A draft in another chat app, or one the mail watch made on the Dashboard, is left out. A draft set for a time says so in the list, and goes out on its own at that time. When you change a draft and send it, or dismiss it, what your agent said about it goes gray, marked Out of date. Ask your agent what is unsent and it counts the email drafts waiting in that conversation. Text drafts are counted only by the line over the box. A chat app shows the card's words, "Not sent yet." included, with no line over the box.

entries.s: Turn on Write like me and give it some of your own writing: your sent mail, a document, or something you paste. When your agent drafts a reply, in chat, to mail that just arrived, or to a text, it writes it the way you write, and a text still reads like a text. You still read every draft before it goes.
entries.x: On the Knowledge tab, under How you write. On the Knowledge tab, open How you write and switch on Write like me. Add your writing with Read my sent mail, Paste something, or Add documents. Press Read my writing. Under Which skills write like me, pick Like me, Its own writing, or Not like me for each skill. Or, after you write your own words on a second draft, press Write like me on its card. It learns only when you press Read my writing. Drafts use it only with Write like me on, your writing read, and that skill not set to Not like me. Warmer, briefer and more formal versions don't use it, and neither does Rewrite it for me. If you let Archie read your sent mail, it keeps the parts you wrote and a short description on this computer, and in backups you make, until you clear them. The description and a few lines of your own writing go to your AI company each time a skill set to write like you does its work. Your samples go each time you press Read my writing. Reading your sent mail asks you first, and can't be done on the free starter credits. The card offers Write like me once, only on an agent whose writing has never been read, and only the owner can press it. On Archie for Teams, a teammate's mailbox gets nobody's style.

entries.s: On a Mac, your agent reads texts as they arrive in Messages and offers a reply on a card when one needs an answer. Nothing sends until you press Send, and a reply goes out from your own number, as if you had typed it.
entries.x: On your agent's Skills tab, under Text Replies: Watch my texts and Open Full Disk Access. Add Text Replies to your agent, then open it on the Skills tab. Switch on Watch my texts. Press Open Full Disk Access and allow Archie in the Mac's System Settings. When a reply card arrives, press Send, Edit it, or Dismiss. The reply card arrives in the chat app your agent uses, so you can press Send from your phone. It works only on a Mac, and never on the free starter credits. It starts when you switch it on and never reads your history on its own. When a new text arrives, it also reads the last 12 messages of that conversation and up to 8 of your own earlier texts, and they go to your AI account with it. To stop that, switch off Read the earlier messages in the conversation. Then a reply can miss what a message refers to. Verification codes, short-code senders, and messages carrying opt-out phrasing like "reply STOP" are dropped on this computer before any AI reads them. Group chats are off until you turn them on. The reply card quotes the message, so it crosses your chat app's servers like anything else you read there. On a shared agent, only the owner can send a reply. A reply with a blank still in it won't send until you fill it in. Archie reads your address book on this computer to turn a number into the name you saved. The name then shows on the card and goes to your AI account with the text.

entries.s: When you type your brokerage, phone number, or business name into a blank on an email draft, the card offers Keep for every draft.
entries.x: On an email draft card, after you fill in a blank with Edit it. Press Edit it on the draft and fill in the blank. Press Keep for every draft. Archie Mobile shows the card's words and buttons. A chat app with no buttons takes the typed words. Email cards only. Text drafts are never filled. If you changed the words around the blank too, no button appears. Only on your own email address.

entries.s: When your agent starts reading your mail, it says in the chat which inboxes it reads and how often, with a Stop watching button.
entries.x: In your agent's chat. The switch it turns off is Watch my inbox, on the agent's Skills tab, under Email Manager. Press Stop watching under the message, or switch off Watch my inbox under Email Manager on the Skills tab. It arrives in your conversation like any message, so it also shows on Archie Mobile or your chat app. It says so once per agent. Switching the watch off and on again does not repeat it. Only the owner can stop it from the button. Not on the free credits or a plan with the AI included, where no AI reads your mail.

entries.t: Mail from people you write to comes first
entries.s: Mail from someone you wrote to in the last two weeks is read at once; other mail can wait a few minutes, which lowers what your AI account is charged.
entries.x: It knows one thing: whether you wrote to the sender in the last 14 days. Replies from Archie's cards count on any account, and Gmail's Sent copies count. A reply sent from Outlook or another mail app is not seen. The addresses you wrote to are kept on your computer and in backups you make. Only on an AI account of your own with Anthropic.

entries.s: Your agent leaves a blank in square brackets, like [her school], for a detail nobody gave, and an email or text with a blank in it will not send.
entries.x: On an email or text card. Press Send and Archie names the blank. Edit it is on the card. Press Edit it on the card. Fill in what goes in the brackets. Press Send. Archie Mobile's Send gives the same answer and puts the buttons back. On a chat app with no buttons, reply "edit it". Leaving a blank is an instruction to the AI, and it can still write a guess as if it were known. Any short words in brackets count, so a [sic] holds Send too. Brackets in your current signature do not. On a card waiting for its time, press Back to draft first, then Edit it. A message written into the chat for you to copy, or one through a connected CRM, is not checked.

entries.s: On an email your agent drafts in chat, a price, a day, or a time that nobody gave it is listed under the draft for you to check.
entries.x: Under the draft on an email card. Press Take out what you added to have Archie rewrite the draft without them. Archie Mobile shows the card's own words, the list included. Code reads amounts, days, times, stock excuses like "something has come up on our end", and a few kinds of promise. Anything else is listed only when your agent names it. It lists them. It does not stop Send. Not on texts, and not on drafts the mail watch writes when mail arrives. A number that appears anywhere in what you gave counts as given, and editing the card's words clears the list.

entries.s: Ask your agent to text a lead, and it writes the text, says whether they agreed to texts, and puts a button under it so you can send it yourself.
entries.x: Under your agent's reply in Chat: Copy the text. Ask your agent to text a lead by name. Press Copy the text, or Open in Messages on your phone. Press Send in Messages yourself. Archie Mobile shows Open in Messages, which opens Messages to their number with the words typed in. A chat app gets the words and no button. Archie sends no text. You press Send on your own phone. It reads what the Texting column says, which someone wrote down. It does not enforce consent. Only where a list keeps a Texting column, which today is the real estate setup's People. If they said stop, it writes no text.

entries.s: Before your agent reads an email, Archie checks whether you have the sender written down on your lists, on your agent, in what you have told your agent about your work, or as someone you wrote to lately.
entries.x: It changes how their mail is read. Only people you wrote to in the last 14 days skip the wait. A match by full name or by a company's address can be wrong. One-word names are never matched, and a first name in your notes counts only for someone with your last name. A known sender's mail in a Gmail tab like Promotions is read, which is one more read on your AI account.

entries.t: An email offers the change to your list
entries.s: When an email says something new about an entry on one of your lists, your agent puts the change on a card, and nothing changes until you press Update.
entries.x: A card in your chat with your agent, after an email arrives. Read what the entry says now, what the email says, and the email's own words on the card. Press Update to change the entry, or Leave it to keep it as it is. Archie Mobile shows the same card, with Update and Leave it. Only an entry the email names by its name, like Netflix or Blue Cross. It never adds an entry. One email is read against one entry, so an email about two units names one of them. Each email that names an entry is one read on your AI account, up to four an hour. Only where your chat has buttons. A chat app without them gets no card. A card still waiting after a week is cleared.

entries.t: A price nobody gave is left as a blank
entries.s: If a draft quotes a price not in what you typed, your lists, your files, or the email it answers, it is left in brackets and Send waits.
entries.x: Dollar amounts only. "140 dollars" in words is not read as a price. A made-up price that happens to match a number you gave is not held. Files over 24KB are checked only when your agent read them on that turn. A draft written on its own, that you did not ask for, quotes a price only if you wrote it down or it is in that conversation.

entries.t: A sent draft says it went
entries.s: Your agent's own words are never changed. When you press Send on an email it drafted, Archie says it went under the message that came with the draft: "Sent to Ace Septic at 8:01am."
entries.x: Under your agent's message, in your chat with it. On an iPhone, Archie Mobile shows the same line under the message. It says Archie sent it. It does not say it arrived or was read. Email drafts shown in the chat only. A text draft, a draft the mail watch wrote on its own, and a catch-up list get no such line. On Telegram, Slack, Discord and Matrix it comes as a short message of its own, which can make your phone buzz on all but Telegram. Signal and iMessage get no extra line. Your agent is told a reply went out when you pressed or typed Send, and is not told when one went at a time you set.

entries.s: When your agent wants to add, move or delete an event on a calendar you connected, it shows you the exact change and makes it only after you approve it in a later message. The exception is Yes, and stop asking, for some changes to your own calendar.
entries.x: In your chat with your agent, on the card that shows the change, with Confirm, Change something and Cancel. Ask your agent for the change, such as "Move my 2:00 with Dana to Thursday." Read the change on the card. Press Confirm, or say yes in your own words. Press Change something to say what should be different, or Cancel. The same card reaches Archie Mobile and chat apps with buttons, and a press there approves the same way. On Signal, iMessage and Matrix, reply in words. A routine running on its own can't change your calendar at all. It reports the change it would have made instead. After you press Yes, and stop asking, your agent adds and moves events on your own calendar that nobody else is on without asking. It tells you each one, with Undo on the line over the message box. Deleting an event, inviting someone, and changing an event other people are on always wait for your yes. A message that only says thanks leaves the change waiting. Ok, okay or sounds good on its own approves it. Your agent judges whether your reply was a yes. Archie makes sure the yes comes in a later message than the change. Reading your calendar needs no approval. An approval protects you only if you read the change before you approve it.

entries.t: Your calendar is checked before a reply about a time
entries.s: When a text or an email asks about a time, your agent looks at your calendar before it writes the reply, so the draft won't say yes to a time you're already booked. When it offers to put something on your calendar, it tells you if that time is already taken.
entries.x: There is no switch. The draft's card says your calendar was checked first, and a booking your agent proposes says if it overlaps something. Only a message that names a time in words it recognizes, such as a weekday, 3pm, 10/12, lunch or a call. "Are you around later?" is drafted without your calendar. Only the next 14 days are checked. It warns and stops nothing. A booking that overlaps can still be approved, and a draft can still be changed to say yes. It reads one calendar on each connected account, usually the main one, and never the other person's. Holidays, birthdays and calendars shared into your account are left out. The draft is written knowing when you are busy, never what the event is, unless the person you are answering is on it. For a booking, an all-day entry such as a trip or a birthday does not count as a clash. On Archie for Teams, a teammate's mailbox is checked against that teammate's calendars and the business's shared ones. Text Replies needs a Mac, because it reads the Messages app.

entries.t: Invitations and a place on an event
entries.s: When your agent sets up a meeting, it can put the place on it and invite people once you say yes. The change it shows you first names everyone who will get an invitation, by name and email address.
entries.x: In your chat with your agent, on the calendar change it proposes. Once you say yes, your calendar sends the invitations. Ask your agent to set up a meeting, and say where it is and who should come. Read the place and the guests on the change, and check any address it points out. Press Confirm, or say yes. On an iPhone, from Archie Mobile 1.4, the waiting change shows its whole sentence, so every guest is listed. The Android download is older and lacks this. Nobody is invited before your yes, and a routine running on its own can't invite anyone. Inviting someone always waits, even after Yes, and stop asking. If your agent wrote an address it did not find in your mail, your lists, or what you told it, the change asks you to check that address first. An address found in your mail can still belong to the wrong person. Your agent sees when other people are busy, never what they are doing. That works on a work or school Outlook account, and on a Google account connected or reconnected since Archie 0.3.11 or connected to look only. To reconnect a Google account, on the Connections tab, under Email, calendar, files, press Reconnect. Where your agent can't see someone, it says so and offers you times to send them. A personal Outlook.com account can't look, and people outside your organization usually can't be seen. Adding someone to an existing meeting also tells the people already on it. Still done in your calendar app: taking someone off, a video link, answering an invitation, and an all-day or repeating event. No invitation has been tried yet on iCloud or another calendar connected with an app password. It has never been run against a real Google, Outlook or iCloud account.

entries.t: Ask what's on, what's due, or what's free
entries.s: Ask about some days and Archie hands your agent what your lists, your calendar, and your reminders hold for those days before it answers.
entries.x: Ask your agent a question that names a day and the schedule, such as "What's on Saturday?" or "What's due this week?" Your agent answers from your lists, your calendar, and your reminders, and says where each thing came from. A question typed on a chat app or in Archie Mobile gets the same kind of answer, because the computer running Archie gathers it. It goes by the words of a question you type. "Am I around Friday?" has no schedule word, and routines and the mail and text watches never get it. What is free works only on lists shaped like the restroom trailer and portable restroom setups, and it goes by the day, never the hour. It reads what is written on your lists and one calendar on each connected account. A booking that is only in an email or a text is left out. What it finds for those days goes to your AI company with your question.

entries.t: Dates from your lists on the Calendar
entries.s: The Calendar tab shows the dates on your lists beside your calendar events, reminders, and routines, so a booking kept on a list shows on its day.
entries.x: On your agent's Calendar tab, marked On your lists in the legend. Press a date's title and that list opens. Open your agent's Calendar tab. Look for the dates marked On your lists, at the head of each day. Press one to open its list. In Archie Mobile, the Calendar under More shows the same dates for the next seven days, and pressing one opens Lists rather than that one list. Pressing a list date opens the list and changes nothing. Which dates count is read off the column names, so a list whose names are misread can show an old date or hide a coming one. Birthdays and anniversaries come round every year. The computer shows a week at a time. The phone shows the next seven days and does not move.

entries.t: A stop moved onto a busy day
entries.s: Move a stop to a day its truck or driver is on your calendar for something else, or a day that job already has a stop. Your agent tells you what is there and asks before moving it.
entries.x: In your chat with your agent, with Move it anyway and Pick another day under its question. Press Move it anyway, or Pick another day. Only lists with a Driver or Truck column, and only when a stop's day moves. It looks for the driver's or truck's name in your calendar's event titles. "Mike out" names Mike; "Dentist, 9am" does not. A driver's working hours, and other stops that day, are not checked. Only on a message you typed. A routine moving a stop is not held.

entries.t: Where Bookings and your calendar differ
entries.s: On an event trailer agent, the morning list compares your Bookings list with your calendar for today and the next two weeks, and says where one has a booking the other does not. Ask what is on a day and your agent says the same.
entries.x: In the morning list, and in your agent's answers about a day. It only reads. It changes neither Bookings nor your calendar, and you decide which is right. Only clear differences are said. Anything within two days of a booking, part of a name, or a calendar that did not answer is left out. The calendar side needs the customer's whole name, or the booking's event name with their last name. Only the event trailer setup's Bookings list, and only your own calendar.

entries.t: Your to-do list on the Dashboard
entries.s: Your to-do list is the first thing on your agent's Dashboard, where you can tick something off or add one without asking your agent.
entries.x: On the agent's Dashboard tab, the first card, with Add a to-do at the bottom. Open your agent's Dashboard. Tick a to-do to mark it done, or type one in Add a to-do. Archie Mobile shows the same list first on the Dashboard, where you can tick to-dos off and add new ones. Only on an agent with the Task Manager add-on. To-dos kept in Todoist or Google Tasks do not show here. Something waiting on you, like a draft to send, sits above it. A checklist your agent already posted in the chat updates only when your agent next touches the list. Change a date or a priority by telling your agent, or in the list on the Knowledge tab.

entries.s: A list can show its steps, like Quoted, Booked, Out and Picked up, with each entry's step in color and a count at each step.
entries.x: On the Knowledge tab, under Lists, under Stages on the list's own form. Open the list on the Knowledge tab, under Lists. Under Stages, pick the choice column that holds the steps. Or ask your agent to turn a list's steps on. Archie Mobile shows the count at each step under Lists, in the same colors, and on iPhone opens a list's entries to add or change them. Nothing enforces the steps. An entry can skip one, and moving an entry starts nothing by itself.

entries.t: Lists in the sidebar and on the Dashboard
entries.s: Keep up to six lists in your agent's sidebar, under Jobs, and each one shows on the Dashboard with its count and where its entries stand.
entries.x: On the list, press Keep in the sidebar. Kept lists show in the sidebar after Jobs and as tiles on the Dashboard. Open a list on the Knowledge tab, under Lists. Press Keep in the sidebar. Archie Mobile lists the kept lists after Jobs on More. Up to six lists. On Archie for Teams, keeping a shared list in one agent's sidebar puts it in nobody else's.

entries.t: Lists made from what you tell your agent
entries.s: When you first set up your agent and say what work you do, it drafts up to three lists that work runs on, with their steps.
entries.x: Answer your agent's first questions about your work. It drafts lists only from what you said, and only when your work comes in rows. It happens at the first questions. An agent set up earlier does not get lists by itself. On the free credits and the plan with the AI included, nobody has yet seen it work on a real account.

entries.s: The last of your agent's first questions is where you keep your work today, with a button for each place, and its goodbye offers a way to bring in each of the first two.
entries.x: Under the goodbye in your agent's chat: Add the spreadsheet, It's on another computer, Add the exported file, Add a photo of a page, Connect my calendar, or Connect Follow Up Boss. Press each place you keep your work, then press That's all when you are done. Press the button under the goodbye and pick the file or photo. Press Send, then press Add on the card when the entries look right. In Archie Mobile, the file and photo buttons open the phone's file picker or camera. There is no calendar button there, and chat apps show no button. It opens a picker. You choose and send the file, and nothing is added until you press a button on its card. In your head, somewhere else, or a skipped answer gets no button, except a realtor's Tell me your open deals. Other software means an exported file, unless you named Follow Up Boss. Two ways in at most. A third place gets no button under the goodbye.

entries.t: Bring in a spreadsheet someone emailed
entries.s: Say "bring in the spreadsheet Dana emailed", and your agent finds the email, opens the file, and puts its rows on a card for you to add.
entries.x: In your agent's chat. When your work is in a spreadsheet, the goodbye of the first questions also has It's on another computer. Ask your agent to bring in the spreadsheet somebody emailed you. Look over the rows on the card, then press its button to add them. Ask from Archie Mobile the same way, or press + and then Choose a file to send one yourself. Only on an AI account of your own with your mail connected. Otherwise, Archie says how to save the file and send it in the chat. Nothing reaches the other person, and nothing is added until you press a button. It has not opened a file from a real mailbox yet.

entries.s: Ask who owes you money, and your agent answers from entries on your lists marked billed and not paid, oldest first, with the days each has waited.
entries.x: In your agent's chat. Ask "Who owes me money?", "Who hasn't been billed yet?", or "Who still owes a deposit?" Ask from Archie Mobile or a chat app, and the answer arrives like any reply. It reads your own lists. It does not connect to QuickBooks or any accounting app. It knows what was written down: an entry counts as owed because its billing says Billed. A deposit is read from a booking's stage and its Deposit column. Nothing records the money arriving. It answers this way only when the question uses words like owe, unpaid, overdue, or invoice.

entries.t: Fixing a save your agent claimed but never made
entries.s: If a reply says it put something on your lists and nothing was saved, Archie adds a line saying so, with Save it to save it now.
entries.x: Under your agent's reply in Chat. Press Save it, or Save to and the list's name, or reply "save it" where there is no button. The line is part of the reply, and Archie Mobile, Telegram, Slack, and Discord show Save it. It catches certain words in a sentence about a list. A claim worded another way passes. Only claims about lists are corrected. "I've updated your calendar" or a note about you gets no line. No Save it button on Signal, iMessage, or Matrix. Save it is a request: your agent saves on that turn, with the usual Undo. A reply that answers where things are kept, like "where does this save", is not corrected (from 0.3.12 on a Mac).

entries.t: A new list takes its first entries
entries.s: Ask for a new list and say what goes on it in the same message, and your agent makes the list and adds those entries in one reply.
entries.x: In your agent's chat. Ask for the list and name its first entries in one message. It works the same from Archie Mobile or a chat app. Making a list is for the owner, or a teammate allowed to act as the owner. This is about an agent's first list. An agent that already has a list could always add entries at once.

entries.s: Ask your agent who to call, and Archie works it out from your People and Deals lists: birthdays, closing anniversaries, quiet leads, and past clients.
entries.x: In your agent's chat. Ask "Who should I call this week?" or "Which leads have gone quiet?" Ask from Archie Mobile or a chat app, and the answer arrives like any reply. Only lists called People, Deals, Your leads, and Listings are read, which the real estate setup and Lead Desk make. It knows what was written down. An empty Last contact means nobody wrote one, even if you did talk. Only an email reply sent through Archie updates Last contact. Texts, calls, and other mail do not. Someone marked Said stop is listed as call or email only. Nothing blocks a text to them.

entries.s: When your agent adds someone, Archie looks on your lists for the same phone number, email, or name, and your agent says who it may be.
entries.x: In your agent's chat, after it adds an entry. It works the same from Archie Mobile or a chat app. It adds first and asks after. Nothing is merged or refused. Only entries your agent adds one at a time are checked, not ones from the Lists screen, an import, or a card. A shared last name is enough only when one of the two has no phone and no email. On a list with a day on every entry, like Expenses, the same name on another day is not named, since that is a second visit (from 0.3.12 on a Mac).

entries.t: Hear when a booking puts something in two places
entries.s: When a booking puts a trailer or a unit in two places on the same day, Archie saves it as asked and says which booking it runs into.
entries.x: On your agent's Knowledge tab, under Lists, the note after Added or Saved says it. A card's Add and the chat's import card say it too. Nothing stops the booking. It is saved as you asked or typed it, and you decide which one changes. Only lists shaped like the two rental setups are checked, by the day and never the hour. A tech sent to two jobs at once is not caught. When your agent saves the booking itself, you hear about it only if its reply says so. More than 200 entries added at once are not checked, and the note says to look over the busy days on the Calendar tab instead.

entries.t: Bring a spreadsheet into a list
entries.s: Import a spreadsheet into one of your lists. Archie matches the columns, leaves out rows already there, and names every cell it could not read.
entries.x: On your agent's Knowledge tab, under Lists, open a list and press Import beside Add row. An empty list also says Have a spreadsheet of these already? Import it. Open the list on your agent's Knowledge tab, under Lists. Press Import, then pick a file on this computer or a Google Sheet shared with your agent. Under Match your columns, give each column of the file a place on the list, Leave it out, or Add it as a new column. Read what will be added and what will be left out, then press Add, or Match while the box to keep it matched is checked. To take it all back, press Undo, here or on the job on the Jobs tab. The box to keep the list matched to the file starts checked. Uncheck it and the list is a copy taken once. Archie never changes your file. Taken as a copy, it adds and never updates. A row that repeats an entry is left out and never used to change it. One tab, up to 5,000 rows and 20 MB. A Numbers file has to be saved as Excel or CSV first. Dates are read month first, so 3/10/2026 meant as October 3 comes in as March 10.

entries.t: Drop a spreadsheet in the chat
entries.s: Drop a spreadsheet into the chat and Archie puts up a card that names the list it fits and how many rows would come in.
entries.x: In the chat with your agent, in Archie or on a chat app that shows buttons. Drop a spreadsheet into the chat, with or without a few words. On the card, press Add, choose A different list, press Make a new list from it, or press Just keep the file. Look the rows over on the card that comes up below, change or uncheck any, then press Add. On Telegram, Slack or Discord, a spreadsheet you send gets the same card with its buttons. Words that do more than hand the file over start an ordinary reply too, and your agent may open the file, which sends what it reads to your AI company. Columns are matched by name only. The card names any column the list has no place for, and Make a new list keeps them all. The first sheet only, up to 5,000 rows and 10 MB. Sent through a chat app, the file passes through that app's servers on its way.

entries.t: Check new entries on one card before Add
entries.s: Hand your agent a photo, a page, or your calendar, and every entry it finds for one of your lists goes on one card you check before anything is added.
entries.x: On the card in the chat with your agent. It also waits on the Jobs tab, in the Needs you column, with Approve and No thanks. Send a photo or a page, paste a list, or ask your agent to go through your calendar for one of your lists. On the card, uncheck any entry to leave it off, or press Change to fix one. Press Add, or tell your agent yes. Pressing Not now leaves them all off. Undo on the card takes the whole card back off the list. The entries are what the AI read, which can be wrong. The card is there so you check them. Only entries on the card are held back. One more entry you tell your agent while it waits goes in at once. Add needs the agent running. A card waits two weeks at most and goes away with New chat. Reading a photo sends it to the AI company that reads pictures for your agent.

entries.t: Bring a shared Google Sheet into a list
entries.s: Ask your agent to bring a Google Sheet you shared with it into one of your lists. The rows come in on a card you check first.
entries.x: Share the Sheet on your agent's Connections tab, under Email, calendar, files, in Google's own file picker. On your agent's Connections tab, under Email, calendar, files, pick the Sheet in Google's file picker. Ask your agent to bring that sheet into one of your lists. Check the card, then press Add or say yes. It is a copy taken when you ask, unless you press the button that offers to keep the list matched to the Sheet. Nothing is ever written to the Sheet. Only a Sheet you picked, one tab at a time, up to 5,000 rows. Columns are matched by their names, and the card cannot change the match. It has not yet been run against a live Google account.

entries.t: How far along a list is
entries.s: Tell Archie about how many a list will hold, and it shows how many are entered so far, such as 25 of about 300 units entered.
entries.x: On the list's page, press the pencil to edit the list and fill in About how many in all, once everything is entered. Or tell your agent in the chat. Open the list on your agent's Knowledge tab, under Lists. Press the pencil to edit the list. Fill in About how many in all, and save. Or tell your agent, for example "We run about 300 units." Archie Mobile's list tiles show the same count. The number is yours. Nothing counts your units anywhere but the list. It is read from your words, so "three hundred units" spelled out is missed. The list's form shows the number and changes it.

entries.t: Fold a row listed twice into one
entries.s: When a unit number or another value meant to be on a list once shows up twice, the list says so, and Review keeps the row you pick.
entries.x: On the list's page, in the line Listed more than once under the column's name, with Review. Open the list on your agent's Knowledge tab, under Lists. Press Review on the Listed more than once line. Press Keep this one on the row to keep. To put both rows back, press Undo on that job on the Jobs tab. It happens only when you press it, and only in Archie on the computer. Where both rows have a value, the kept row's wins. Only long notes are joined. It finds a repeat only under a column meant to hold each value once, such as Unit number.

entries.t: Ask about a unit by number
entries.s: Ask about unit 31 and your agent finds the row titled S-31, matching names like Trailer 4 or INV-1042 by their letters and numbers.
entries.x: It only helps your agent find the row. Nothing stops it changing the wrong one. It works on rows whose titles read like a code: three words at most, ending in a number. A date, a time or an amount never counts.

entries.t: Keep a list matched to its spreadsheet
entries.s: Keep your own spreadsheet, and the list you brought in from it stays matched: Archie changes the list when you save the file, never changes your file, and asks before taking an entry off.
entries.x: On your agent's Knowledge tab, under Lists, when you import a spreadsheet: the box Keep Units matched to units.xlsx, with your list's and file's names. The list's page then says what it matches. Import a file on this computer, or a Google Sheet shared with your agent, into a list. Leave the box to keep it matched checked, and press Match. Save the file as you always do. The list changes to match. When entries are no longer in the file, press Take them off or Keep them on the list's page. On an iPhone, Archie Mobile shows a matched list and can take entries off with the same Undo. Matching is turned on at the computer. Archie only reads the file. A file on this computer is looked at every minute while your agent runs; a Google Sheet every 15 minutes and before the morning list. Nothing is checked while your agent is stopped or the computer running Archie is off. Only Google Sheets you picked on the Connections tab, under Add files. One tab of a workbook, up to 5,000 rows. A file over 20 MB is not read.

entries.t: A late pickup, asked about once a day
entries.s: Archie asks you about a late pickup for a rental at most once a day in the same chat, unless you bring that rental up.
entries.x: In your chat with your agent, for rentals past their end date. Only rentals past their end date whose stage says the units are still out. One chat, and one day on the computer's clock. It still says the rental is late. Only the question is not asked again.

entries.t: Matching entries, added up in code
entries.s: When Archie looks up entries on one of your lists and two or more match, code adds up the number columns, like units and price. Your agent gets the totals, so it does not add them itself.
entries.x: In your agent's answers about your lists. Only when every match is in the result, up to 200. A lookup that left some out is not added up. Number columns only, judged by the column's name. An id, phone number, ZIP code, year, stop number, score or rate per unit is never added. A total that some entries leave blank says how many entries it is from. Your agent can still say another number, and the total is not on the Read line under the reply.

entries.t: Units out, counted place by place
entries.s: When Archie looks up the units you have out, code counts them place by place against the rentals running there today. Your agent hears where your two lists agree, where they differ, and by how many.
entries.x: In your agent's answers about your units and rentals. Only for a list of units with a place column and a dated list of rentals with a count and a place of its own. Trailers booked by name are not counted this way. Places match by the words typed, so "Oak Hollow #12" and "Oak Hollow lot 12" are two places. It compares counts, never unit numbers, and it does not say which list is right. A teammate who sees only some rows does not get it.

entries.s: A reminder you ask for also goes on your to-do list; tick it off and the reminder is not said, and deleting it in one place removes both.
entries.x: On the Dashboard's to-do list, on the Calendar, and on the reminder's card in the chat. Ask your agent to remind you of something. To drop it, press Delete under the reply that set it, on the Dashboard, on the Calendar, or on the card when it goes off. In Archie Mobile on iPhone, swipe left on the to-do list or press Delete on the Calendar. Only on an agent with the Task Manager add-on. Promises caught from texts show on the list only with Commitment Keeper as well. Nobody has watched it in the Archie window yet.

entries.s: When a reminder goes off, Remind me later offers in an hour, this evening or tomorrow, each with its time on the button, or another time in your words.
entries.x: On the reminder's card in the chat. When a reminder goes off, press Remind me later. Pick In an hour, This evening, Tomorrow or Another time, or press Back. Nobody has watched it in the Archie window yet.

entries.t: Your agent works while you are away
entries.s: Your agent runs routines, reads new mail, and reports to you with nobody watching, for as many hours as your computer is on and Archie is open.
entries.x: Routine reports and replies reach your chat app or Archie Mobile while the computer running Archie is on. Your computer has to be on with Archie open. While it is off, your agent answers nothing. Archie has no working-hours setting. The hours are whenever your computer is on and Archie is open. A routine can wake a sleeping computer. A computer that is shut down stays off. Mail that arrived while the computer was off is read when it is back on, within a limit.

entries.s: For a line of work Archie has a setup for, your agent can send what is on today each morning, built from your lists without asking an AI.
entries.x: On the Routines tab, the Morning list row has its switch. Your agent also offers it at the end of your first evening. Say yes when your agent offers it at the end of your first evening, or switch on Morning list on the Routines tab. Or say "send me the morning list" in the chat. Press Another time under the offer to pick a time before noon, or say "send me the morning list at 6:30am". To stop it, press Stop on the list, or say "stop the morning list". It arrives in your chat with your agent, and Archie Mobile's Routines screen has the same Morning list switch. Only for the lines of work Archie has a setup for: portable restrooms, home trades, event trailers and real estate. It comes only after you say yes, and only on mornings with something on it. It needs Archie running and your computer awake at some point between its time and noon. A computer asleep until after noon gets none that day. It goes only to your own chat with your agent. Your team does not see it.

entries.t: Waking the computer for a routine
entries.s: A routine set for seven in the morning arrives at seven, even if your computer was asleep. Archie wakes it a few minutes before, runs it, and lets it sleep.
entries.x: On the Routines tab, a routine that missed a run while your computer slept shows Wake this computer. Press it, then Set this up. On the Routines tab, open a routine that missed a run while your computer slept. Press Wake this computer, then Set this up. On a Mac, type your password in macOS's own box. Archie never sees what you type. On Windows it is one press, with nothing to approve. It wakes a sleeping computer. One that is shut down stays off, so choose Sleep instead of Shut Down. On a Mac, setting it up asks for an administrator's password once. On Windows, the power plan has to allow wake timers. If it does not, the routine shows the steps to change it. Only a routine set for a time of day wakes your computer. One that runs every few minutes does not.

entries.t: Missed routines run when the computer wakes
entries.s: A routine due while your computer was asleep runs when it wakes, as long as that is the same morning, afternoon, or evening. Past that, its row says it missed.
entries.x: The line under the Routines tab's title says this, and a routine that missed a run says so on its row. Past noon for a morning, 6:00 PM for an afternoon, or midnight for an evening, the run is recorded as missed and not run. After your computer sleeps through several of a day's times, the routine runs the latest one, once. Routines run from the computer running Archie. A computer that is shut down runs nothing.

entries.t: One routine at several times a day
entries.s: A routine can run at several set times a day, up to 24, like 9:00 in the morning and 5:00 in the afternoon.
entries.x: On the Routines tab, open a routine and press Add a time. You can also set the times in the chat. Open the routine on the Routines tab. Press Add a time and pick the time. Or tell your agent in the chat, like "run it at 9:00am and 5:00pm". Archie Mobile shows every time a routine runs at and can move any one of them. Up to 24 set times a day. More often than that is an interval, like every 30 minutes, which counts from when it starts. Each time it runs counts as a job. On the free tier, at most 15 of a routine's runs happen in a day. After your computer sleeps through several of a day's times, it runs the latest one, once.

entries.s: Tell your agent to remind you at a time, and it does, in your own words, at that minute, without asking an AI anything to read it back.
entries.x: In the chat. Reminders also show on the Jobs tab and the Calendar tab, and on the to-do list on an agent with the To-Do List. Say "remind me at 3pm to call the dentist". When it goes off, press Done, Remind me later, or Delete. To cancel early, press Delete under the reply that set it. Archie Mobile notifies you once notifications are on in its Settings, and a chat app shows the buttons where it can draw them. Otherwise a reminder waits in the chat until you open it. One reminder is one moment. Something every week is a routine. Quiet hours do not hold a reminder back, since you named the minute. One whose minute passed while your computer slept arrives when it wakes, saying when it was for. Past a week it is dropped.

entries.t: A reminder that stands down when the person writes back
entries.s: Make a reminder conditional, like "remind me Thursday to chase the quote unless Ellen has replied". If Ellen emails or texts in first, it is dropped and Archie tells you.
entries.x: In the chat. The condition shows beside the reminder on the Jobs tab and in the list. Add "unless Ellen has replied" to a reminder you ask for, naming the person. It notices only that Ellen wrote. A note from her about something else also drops the reminder. It needs a mailbox connected or the Mac text watch. With neither, the reminder simply arrives at its time, and your agent says so. A name matches as a whole word, and an address matches exactly.

entries.s: When your agent posts on its own, like a reminder or a routine's report, your computer shows an alert with the agent's name and the first line.
entries.x: Settings, General, Show alerts on this computer. It is on from the start. To turn it off, open Settings, then General, and switch off Show alerts on this computer. This alert is on your computer only. Archie Mobile has its own notifications, once you turn them on in its Settings. It shows only while Archie is open behind your other windows, on a computer that is on and awake. Clicking the alert does not open the conversation. Archie cannot tell whether your computer blocks its alerts, so the Settings row says where your computer's own switch is. A reminder within 60 seconds of a conversation ending, on an agent with a chat app, raises no alert.

entries.s: A day after your first evening, an agent with the journal offers once to ask you one question about your day at 9:30pm, and your answer goes in the journal.
entries.x: In your agent's chat. Press Yes, at 9:30pm to add it, or No thanks. Each evening's question uses a little of your AI. It is offered once, and never to an agent set up before this change. Archie only. Archie for Teams has no journal.

entries.t: Today's Calendar skips an empty day
entries.s: On a morning with nothing on your calendar, the store's Today's Calendar routine sends nothing and uses none of your AI. Press Run now and it still answers.
entries.x: The Today's Calendar routine, on your agent's Routines tab. Only Today's Calendar as the store ships it. One you wrote with the same name, or one set to do more than read the calendar, runs as before. A calendar that cannot be read within 20 seconds is not an empty day, and the routine runs. Other routines do not skip empty days.

entries.s: The Knowledge tab opens like folders: Documents your agent reads, Lists it keeps up to date, Memory, and How you write.
entries.x: On the agent's Knowledge tab. Archie Mobile groups documents by the same folders. Documents are files your agent reads and never changes.

entries.s: When you first open Archie, your agent asks a few questions about your work, starting with the first thing you say, so it can help you better.
entries.x: On the first run, in the agent's chat: the card Let me tell you what I do (on Archie for Teams, Let me tell you about the business and my team), and Stop the questions. Press Let me tell you what I do, or just type. Answer its questions. If your first message asks for something, your agent does that first. Press Stop the questions to end them early. The first run happens on the computer. On a chat app, the questions start when you claim your agent. With Archie Mobile alone, they go on in Archie, and Archie Mobile shows the same conversation, so you can answer there. Whether your first message asks for something is the AI's judgment, so it can miss. Asking again gets it done. Your answers go to your AI company like any message. It stops after 12 messages, a second job, a question of yours, or Stop the questions, and keeps what was said by then. On the free tier its own turns are not counted, but a job asked for in your first message is one of the day's 20.

entries.s: At the top of an agent's Knowledge tab, Archie counts its lists, documents, and things it remembers about you, and shows the latest list changes with Undo.
entries.x: At the top of the agent's Knowledge tab, headed with the agent's name, such as What Ember keeps. Open the agent's Knowledge tab. Under Saved lately, press Open or Undo beside a change. Archie Mobile's Documents screen opens with the same three counts, without Saved lately. Saved lately shows list changes only: the five newest not yet taken back. Entries added from a card or an import are not in it. Undo those on the Jobs tab. Undo after forgetting a memory line puts it back as a new line, dated this month.

entries.t: What your agent remembers about you
entries.s: Your agent keeps a short list of what it has learned about you. You can read every line, add one, change one, or delete one.
entries.x: On your agent's Knowledge tab, under Memory. Each line has a pencil, Change this, and a cross, Forget this, and Clear all is at the bottom. Open your agent's Knowledge tab and choose Memory. Press the pencil beside a line to change it, or the cross to forget it. Type in the box to add a line yourself. On the owner's phone, Archie Mobile shows the same Memory under More, then Documents, while the computer running Archie is on. It carries only what has come up lately. Older lines go to a file it looks back at when your words match one. The look back is a match on words, with no AI call of its own. What it remembers goes to your AI company with your messages. The file is on your computer, and Otian AI cannot see it.

entries.t: Bring in what ChatGPT, Claude or Gemini knows about you
entries.s: Archie gives you one sentence to send ChatGPT, Claude or Gemini. Paste its answer back, tick the lines to keep, and your agent remembers them.
entries.x: On your agent's Knowledge tab, under Memory, press Bring in what it knows about you. In Archie, the first setup screen also has a card, Bring in what ChatGPT knows. On your agent's Knowledge tab, under Memory, press Bring in what it knows about you. Copy the sentence Archie gives you and send it to ChatGPT, Claude or Gemini. Paste its answer back and press Show me the lines. Tick the lines to keep and press Remember these. On the owner's phone, Archie Mobile has the same screen under More, then Documents, then Memory, while the computer running Archie is on. Archie never talks to ChatGPT, Claude or Gemini. It reads the text you paste, once. About 25 to 30 short facts fit in what it carries. The rest goes to older memory, and the screen shows which before you press. A line with a password, a card number, or a Social Security or account number is never kept. An address or a health detail comes over if you tick it. Kept lines go to your AI company with your messages, as everything in memory does.

entries.s: When your agent saves a note to its memory, a line under its reply names the note, with Open and Undo.
entries.x: Under your agent's reply in Chat. Open goes to Memory on the agent's Knowledge tab. Press Undo to take the note out, or Open to see it in Memory. Archie Mobile's half is waiting on its next build. On a Mac only. Archie on Windows is still on 0.3.11, without it. Notes kept later from older messages are not named here. They show in Memory. Undo works only while the note still reads as saved. If memory has reworded it, find it under Memory and press Forget this. Undo takes out the note only. Anything that saving it set off stays. Chat apps show none of it.

entries.t: Your small files, checked for what you ask
entries.s: When you ask about something, Archie looks through your small files, like a price sheet or a page of notes, for lines that mention it, and hands them to your agent before it answers. No extra AI call is made.
entries.x: Nothing to switch on. It reads the files on your agent's Knowledge tab. It works on messages from your phone too, because the files are read on the computer. Only small files, about 24 KB of text or less and the 20 newest, and at most three lines a message. A longer document is your agent's to open. It compares words, so a line worded differently from your question is missed. What it finds goes to your AI company with your message, like everything else in it. Your agent is told to open the file before saying something is not in it, and it can still skip that.

entries.t: Send files to your agent, and get files back
entries.s: Send your agent photos, a video, a recording or a document in Archie, and it sends files it made back the same way.
entries.x: In the chat, with the Add button beside the message box, or by dropping files on the conversation. Press Add beside the message box, or drag files onto the conversation. Send the message. For a video or a recording, press Watch it or Listen to it on the card, or Skip. Up to four pictures and one video or recording per message. It asks before it watches a video or listens to a recording, and needs the Video Synthesizer add-on to do either. A document you send is kept under General on the Knowledge tab until you remove it. A recording sent through a chat app such as Telegram is heard as you talking and answered, with no notes made.

entries.s: Some PDFs are photographs of a page, such as a scanned statement, a signed contract or a fax, so the file holds no words to read. Switch this on and Archie looks at the pages and writes out what is on them.
entries.x: On the agent's Setup tab, under Response quality: Read PDFs that are scans. On the agent's Setup tab, open Response quality. Check Read PDFs that are scans. Ask about a scanned PDF on an email, or one you added to your agent's Knowledge. It is off until you switch it on, and works only with Claude, by Anthropic. On another AI account the switch does nothing, and the screen says so. Each file costs about a cent or two on your AI account. It reads up to ten pages and 16 MB. It copies what is printed and never guesses. A figure it can't read is written as [unreadable]. With the switch off, your agent says the file is a scan and asks for the original. The pages go to your AI company, the same place your mail goes when you ask about it. Nothing on this computer reads the page.

entries.t: The page an answer came from
entries.s: Ask where a figure came from and your agent can name the page: Archie reads a PDF you gave it as numbered pages, so you can open that page yourself.
entries.x: In the chat, when you ask about a PDF you sent your agent or added to its Knowledge. Ask your agent where a figure or a sentence in a PDF came from. Open that page of the file to check it yourself. Your agent decides whether to name a page, so some answers name none. Page 7 is the file's seventh page, counting any empty pages. A scanned PDF has no text to point to until Read PDFs that are scans is on. What it reads still goes to your AI company, on the account in use.

entries.t: Your whole agent in one backup file
entries.s: Everything you built goes in one file you save where you like, with no key or token in it. Archie can save one every week.
entries.x: On the Account page, under Backups: Save a backup, Save one every week, and Restore a backup. On the Account page, under Backups, press Save a backup and choose where it goes. For one every week, press Choose a folder under Save one every week. Archie keeps the last three. On another computer, sign in as you and use Restore a backup. It is a plain file holding your chats, lists and documents, so keep it somewhere you would keep a tax return. Keys and passwords stay out. On a new computer you get a list of what to connect again. Downloaded tools, Mac permissions and a paired phone do not travel. Browser sign-ins and a Signal link are dropped on a different computer. It opens only in Archie, on a computer signed in as you.

entries.s: Your agent writes the actual file, such as a PDF, a Word file, a spreadsheet or a deck, and tells you where it put it.
entries.x: Files land in Downloads, in the Archie folder. The switch is on your agent's Setup tab, under What it can do. Ask your agent for a file, for example "Put that in a spreadsheet." Find it in the chat, or in Downloads, inside the Archie folder. It chooses the filename and never the folder. Everything goes to Downloads, in the Archie folder, on the computer running Archie. Eleven kinds only: .pdf, .pptx, .xlsx, .csv, .docx, .md, .txt, .json, .html, .ics and .vcf. It never makes video. One file is 5 MB at most.

entries.s: Ask for a PDF and your agent lays it out on your computer, with headings, bullets, page breaks, and real bar, line or pie charts drawn in.
entries.x: Ask your agent for a PDF, for example "Make me a PDF of this month's expenses with a chart." Charts are bars, a line or a pie, one set of numbers each. A bar chart always starts at zero. A pie leaves out any slice at or below zero. With nothing above zero, it lists the numbers instead. A Word file gets a chart's figures written out instead of the picture.

entries.s: Ask for a deck and you get a real PowerPoint file you can open and change, with each heading starting a slide.
entries.x: Ask your agent for a deck, for example "Turn these notes into a five slide deck." It lands in Downloads, in the Archie folder, and is 5 MB at most.

entries.t: Change a spreadsheet, Word file or deck you give it
entries.s: Give your agent a spreadsheet, Word file, deck or text file and ask for a change. Once you confirm, it sends back a changed copy in the same style.
entries.x: Send the file in the chat, or add it on your agent's Knowledge tab, under Documents. Ask for the change, such as a new expense row or a different sentence. Ask how a total is worked out and it reads the formulas. Press Confirm when it shows you the change. Open the changed copy it sends back. Send the file on any chat app except Signal, which sends and receives no files. It changes Archie's copy. The file where you keep it stays as it was. A total that depends on a changed cell updates when the file is next opened in Excel. Until then your agent reads the old total. A row goes at the end of a list. A slide's lines can change, and it cannot add a slide. A PDF, an .xls or an .ods file is only read. Pages, Numbers, Keynote, an older .doc or .ppt, or a file with macros has to be exported first.

entries.s: Your agent can make a picture and send it to you in the conversation, drawn with OpenAI or Google on your own account.
entries.x: If your AI account is with another company, add a Gemini key for pictures on your agent's Setup tab, under Pictures. Ask your agent for a picture, for example "Draw a logo idea for a lawn care business." If your AI account is not OpenAI or Google, first add a Gemini key on your agent's Setup tab, under Pictures. It sends the picture in your chat app or Archie Mobile, and where a chat app cannot take a file, it saves it on the computer and says where. With only a Claude account and no Gemini key for pictures, it cannot draw. Each picture is billed by the AI company that draws it, never on our credits. What you ask for goes to OpenAI or Google, whichever draws it. No video or music.

entries.t: A file opened from an email comes into the chat
entries.s: After your agent opens a file attached to an email, ask for it, like "send me that invoice", and the file itself comes into the conversation you are in. Files your agent sends go out as big as each chat app takes.
entries.x: In the conversation you are in: a chat app, the Archie window, or Archie Mobile. Ask your agent what a file on an email says, so it opens it. Then ask for the file, for example "Send me that invoice." Ask from a chat app or from Archie Mobile, and the file comes into that conversation. On a Mac only. Archie on Windows is still on 0.3.11, without it. Only in the conversation that opened the file, and within an hour of opening it. Only kinds that do not run when opened, like documents, spreadsheets, PDFs and pictures. Any other kind stays in the email, and your agent says so. It comes to you, in your conversation. A file sent to somebody else goes with an email reply, which waits for you to press Send. A file can be 50 MB on Telegram and Matrix, 100 MB on Slack and iMessage, and 25 MB on Discord and in Archie alone. One opened from an email is 25 MB at most. Discord takes 10 MB, so a bigger file comes into Archie's window instead, and the reply on Discord says so. Signal gets no files.

entries.s: With no direct connection, your agent can use a website itself in a browser window on your computer: it reads, clicks and types, and you can watch.
entries.x: On the Connections tab, under Computer control. Switch on Let this agent click and type for you, then add a site. On the Connections tab, open Computer control. Switch on Let this agent click and type for you. Press + Add a website (+ Add a website or app on a Mac) and type the site's address. Sign in yourself in the window that opens, then close it. Ask your agent for the errand in the chat. Tap Press it for me from Archie Mobile or your chat app, and Archie Mobile can switch Computer control, buying, and each site on or off. Signing in to a site happens at your computer. It never types a password, a card you pay with or a sign-in code. Where one is asked for, it stops and hands you the window. Before a press that sends, submits or finalizes something, it sends you the page. Tap Press it for me, or finish it yourself. A purchase needs buying switched on, at a shop you picked, up to a limit you set. Moving money and signing a contract are always yours to press. It is off until you switch it on. Sites under Blocked sites are never opened, and each job stops after the time you set.

entries.s: Send your agent to look around a site before it does anything real there. It clicks through, finishes nothing, and notes how the site is laid out for next time.
entries.x: On the Connections tab, under Computer control, press Practice beside a site you added. On the Connections tab, open Computer control. Press Practice beside a site you added. Or say yes when your agent offers a practice run. It types only in the search box, stays on that one site, and finishes nothing. A practice run does not make a site safe. Every stop still applies on the real errand afterward. It uses your AI like any other job. It starts only when you press Practice or say yes. Nothing explores on its own.

entries.s: Your agent finds the flight in your confirmation email, checks in on the airline's site the day before, takes a free seat, and sends you the boarding pass.
entries.x: Add Flight Check-In from the Marketplace. It works through Computer control, on the Connections tab. Add Flight Check-In from the Marketplace. Switch on Computer control on the Connections tab. Connect the mailbox your flight confirmations arrive in. It buys nothing: not a seat, a bag or priority boarding. If check-in cannot finish without paying, it stops and tells you what is asked for. It checks in only. It does not book, change or cancel a flight. Where an airline wants an account sign-in or sends a code, it hands you the window.

entries.t: Your agent uses apps on a Mac
entries.s: On a Mac, your agent can use the apps you allow, such as Numbers or Preview, without moving your pointer. If you start using that app, it waits for you.
entries.x: On the Connections tab, under Computer control, press + Add a website or app and type the app's name. On the Connections tab, open Computer control and switch on Let this agent click and type for you. Press + Add a website or app and type the app's name. When macOS asks, allow Archie in System Settings. The panel's Open System Settings button takes you there. Ask your agent for the job in the chat. Archie Mobile can switch Computer control and each app on or off. The macOS permission is given at the Mac. Mac only. On Windows, Computer control covers websites. It never uses Terminal, password keepers, System Settings, Mail, Messages, Calendar, or your web browsers, whatever you allow. It never types a password or a card you pay with, and anything it could not undo waits for you. An app that does not describe its window cannot be used yet, and one that draws its own boxes may not take typing. Your agent says so and asks you.

entries.s: Your agent can buy things for you on a website, if you switch that on. It is off until you do. You choose the shops it may buy from, the most it may spend on one order, and the most in total over 1, 7, 14 or 30 days. The limit is checked against the price it reads on the page.
entries.x: On the agent's Connections tab, under Computer control, in Buying. On the agent's Connections tab, open Computer control and find Buying.
