Turn on the switch that lets your agent press Buy, read Before you switch this on, and press I understand, switch it on. Add the shops it may buy from, then set Most for one purchase, Most in total, and how many days the total counts. Ask for the purchase in the chat. At Place order your agent stops and sends you the page, and it presses only after you tap Press it for me. Tap Press it for me in Archie Mobile or your chat app. On a chat app with no buttons, type press it. Every order waits for your tap. Saying buy it or yes in the chat releases nothing. Archie reads the order total off the last page and checks your limit against it. A charge a shop adds after you place the order can still take it over. For a ceiling nobody can get past, give it a card from your bank that works at one shop. It never types a card you pay with, so your card has to be saved at the shop already. A subscription or free trial works the same way, and the card says what it will charge each time and when. Anything outside your limits it will not press at all. It never moves money or signs a contract, tap or not. Shared checkout pages such as PayPal, Shop Pay and Square are refused. Closing or deleting an account can be tapped too, and its card says "This can't be undone." A teammate on a shared agent never buys. A routine can bring you the card, and the tap is still yours. No real purchase has been completed yet.

entries.s: With Call businesses switched on, your agent can phone a business for you, to ask its hours or prices or whether it can fit you in. It shows you the call first, on a card, and nothing dials until you press Place the call.
entries.x: On the agent's Setup tab, under What it can do: Call businesses. Each call comes as a card in the chat with Place the call. Make an account at Bland, add credit, and copy your key from its Settings. On the agent's Setup tab, under What it can do, open Call businesses. Type your first name and your business's name, paste the Bland key, and press Turn on calls. Ask your agent to call a business. Read the card, then press Place the call. On an iPhone, from Archie Mobile 1.4, the call's cards and Place the call work from the phone. From Archie Mobile 1.5 you can also turn calls on there, with Archie 0.3.12 on a Mac. Archie on Windows is still on 0.3.11, without it. It calls businesses only, never a person, and refuses any number on your agent's lists, on a teammate's card, or in your Mac's Messages. For a number you type yourself, the card asks you to press only if it is a business's line. The voice says first that it is an AI assistant calling for you and that the call is transcribed. It never agrees to buy, book or pay, and never gives card or account details. It asks, and you book. Calls are on your own Bland account, which bills you by the minute. It never calls before 8:00am or after 9:00pm where the business is. It makes three calls a day unless you set 1 to 10, and a call lasts ten minutes at most. Calls do not work on the free starter credits. A business that says not to call again is never called again. No real call has been placed yet.

entries.s: Ask for somewhere to eat near the office open at eight, and your agent looks it up on the map: name, street, distance, phone number and hours.
entries.x: It uses TomTom, on the Connections tab under Apps, the same connection that works out when to leave for a drive. Connect TomTom on the Connections tab, under Apps. Its key is free and needs no card. Ask your agent for a place near somewhere. Ask the same way from Archie Mobile or a chat app. The map has no ratings or prices, so your agent does not say what is good or cheap. Hours come from the map, which is sometimes out of date. Every reply has the phone number so you can check. Without the TomTom connection your agent does not offer it.

entries.s: Ask Price Watch to check your prices, and your agent looks up what Shopify stores charge right now, whether it is in stock, and a link to that store's checkout.
entries.x: Add Price Watch from the Marketplace. Add Price Watch from the Marketplace. Ask it to check your prices. Amazon, Walmart and the other big marketplaces are not Shopify stores, so for those it searches the web. It only reads. An order is placed on the store's own page, under the Buying switch. A price is what the store showed at that moment.

entries.t: Your agent takes on the jobs you pick
entries.s: Each agent carries only the add-ons you put on it, so it fits the way you work and a reply costs less than carrying every one.
entries.x: In the Marketplace. Open the Marketplace. Add the add-ons for the jobs you want this agent to do. Archie Mobile can add an add-on to an agent or take one off. There is no figure for how much less a reply costs. With nothing added, your agent still answers questions, sets reminders, remembers what you tell it and keeps files. Every add-on is included with Archie, at no extra price.

entries.s: Every skill, routine, specialist and personality in the store comes with Archie, with no price of its own.
entries.x: In the Marketplace. A new computer does not get your add-ons by itself. Restore a backup, or add them again.

entries.t: Archie asks before an add-on goes on
entries.s: Whenever you add an add-on, anywhere in Archie, Archie asks first. It shows the add-on, the agent it is going on, what it will use, and which of those accounts that agent already has connected. Then you press Install, or Cancel.
entries.x: In the step that opens whenever you add an add-on, from the Marketplace or anywhere else in Archie. Add an add-on from the Marketplace, the Connections tab, or a suggestion on your agent's page. Read what it will use and what comes with it, such as another add-on it is built on, a routine that starts on a schedule, or a download. Press Install, or Cancel. In Archie Mobile, on iPhone and Android, Add shows the same step first. The phone connects nothing, and says where to connect on the computer. It lists what the add-on declares. Mail tools come with your email connection, and Computer control is a switch for the whole agent, so an add-on that lists neither can still use them. Installing connects nothing. Connecting an account is its own step. Your first agent's starter pack, the Researcher included, goes on without this step, and so do up to two add-ons your first answers pick.

entries.t: Written setups for four lines of work
entries.s: Tell Archie you rent portable restrooms or event restroom trailers, run a home trades company, or sell homes, and it starts with that work's lists and a few rules.
entries.x: The rules are on the Personality tab, under Who this agent serves, and the Dashboard card that names the setup opens them. Answer your agent's first questions about what work you do. Change any list or rule by asking your agent. Archie Mobile shows the lists and their counts, and on iPhone opens on the card that names the setup. Only these lines of work and lead generation have written setups. Every other business gets lists drafted from what you tell it. The rules are what your agent is told. You still check what it writes, such as an ad. It does not connect to the software these businesses use. The lists fill from chat, email, your own entries and spreadsheets you bring in. It happens at the first questions, and the match can miss.

entries.t: A written setup for lead generation
entries.s: Tell Archie your business sells leads, calls or booked appointments, and it starts with Clients, Sources and Orders lists and rules about consent and promises to clients.
entries.x: The rules are on the Personality tab, under Who this agent serves. Answer your agent's first questions about what work you do. Only for businesses whose product is leads, calls or appointments. A business buying leads for itself gets no setup. The rules shape what your agent writes. You are still responsible for consent and for what you send.

entries.t: Job Hunt shows where the people you know work
entries.s: Drop in the connections file LinkedIn emails you and Job Hunt shows where the people you know work now, then drafts a note to the right one.
entries.x: With the Job Hunt skill on your agent, drop the file into the chat. Download the connections file LinkedIn emails you. Drop it into the chat, zip and all. Press Add on the card, then See where they work. Ask who you know at a company, and it says who to write to first and drafts the note. You can send the file from Archie Mobile or a chat app as well. It reads a file you drop in and never connects to LinkedIn. A newer file adds new people and leaves the rest as they were. It drafts and never sends. An email draft goes when you press Send, and a LinkedIn note you paste yourself. The file has each person's current employer and title only, and most people have no email address in it. No real LinkedIn export has been brought in yet.

entries.s: An add-on is a text file your agent reads: written instructions plus settings. It brings no code of its own, and nothing in it runs as a program.
entries.x: An add-on can only use tools Archie already has. A new service, tool or screen comes in an Archie update. The one way to give your agent tools Archie never shipped is an app's address for AI assistants, added under Something else on the Connections tab.

entries.t: Ask whether your agent can do something
entries.s: Ask your agent whether it can do something, and it searches the Marketplace's add-ons for one that fits, or offers to write a new skill when none does.
entries.x: In the chat with your agent. Ask in your own words, like "can you keep track of my medications?" Your agent tells you what it found, up to five add-ons. Say yes in your next message to add one, or ask it to write a skill instead. Ask the same way from Archie Mobile or a chat app, then say yes in your next message. It matches words in add-on names and descriptions and reads back up to five, so it can miss the best fit. Nothing is added until you say yes in a later message. It searches the copy of the store Archie had when your agent started. On a shared agent only the owner can add one. Anyone else is told to ask the owner.

entries.t: Write a skill by describing it
entries.s: Say what you wish your agent could do, in your own words. It asks a couple of questions, writes the skill, and shows you a card to keep it.
entries.x: In the chat, or on Build a skill in the agent's sidebar. To fill in the fields yourself, press Build your own on the Skills tab. Tell your agent what you wish it did, like "prep me before a call". Answer its questions. Read the card, which names what it assumed. Press Keep it, or Change something to adjust it. Archie Mobile has a form for writing a skill by hand. A skill you write can only use what Archie can already do: it is instructions plus permission to use existing tools. Skills, routines and specialists can be written this way. Personalities come only from the Marketplace. The form on the Skills tab offers fewer services than the chat does. A skill you write stays on your agent. Getting one into the Marketplace for other people goes through a review we do by hand.

entries.t: Connect a service that is not listed
entries.s: Connect a service Archie does not list, using the web address of its API and your key, then write a skill that tells your agent which addresses to call.
entries.x: On the Connections tab, under Apps, press Something else at the foot of the list. On the Connections tab, open Apps and press Something else. Give it a name, the web address of its API, and the key that service gave you. Write a skill that uses it, and tell your agent which addresses to call. It works with a service that answers over https and takes a key. A service that will not give you a key cannot be connected this way. Archie knows only the address and the key. You supply the paths in the skill. Reading runs on its own. Anything that changes something waits for your yes, and that cannot be switched off.

entries.s: Add each class's syllabus and your agent tracks the term: what is due this week, what you need on the final, and the school's own deadlines two weeks ahead.
entries.x: Add My Classes and Class Planner from the Marketplace (the College pack has both), then add each syllabus on the agent's Knowledge tab. Add My Classes from the Marketplace. Add each class's syllabus on the Knowledge tab. If you like, paste your class calendar link from your school's site. At registration time, give Class Planner your degree audit. It never turns work in, registers you, or drops a class. It cannot see grades in your school's system, open seats, a waitlist, or a hold on your account. The class calendar link carries only what a professor put a date on. The syllabus is the better source. Reading your school's emails needs a mailbox connected, and the starter credits cannot read mail.

entries.t: What the first run says before connecting
entries.s: On the first run, before you connect a calendar or count your inbox, your agent says what it will read, where that goes, and how to disconnect it later.
entries.x: On the first run, on the Which calendar? and Which email? panels. On the first run, press the calendar or inbox card. Read what your agent says it will read, then pick your account. Connected this way, the calendar is read only. To let your agent change events, press Reconnect on the account's row and check that box. The inbox count asks no AI, but the count then sits in your conversation, which your agent can read back later. The trash can takes the account off your agent. Its sign-in stays under Settings, Saved keys, and Google or Microsoft keeps its permission until you remove it in that account. If the first run connected nothing, it offers Connect my email, Connect my calendar, and Not now once. After Not now, use the Connections tab.

entries.s: When your agent says your calendar, your email, or an app is not connected, a button under its reply opens the Connections tab with the sign-in ready.
entries.x: Under your agent's reply in Chat, such as Connect my calendar or Connect Follow Up Boss. It opens the agent's Connections tab. Press the Connect button under the reply. Pick your account and sign in, in your browser, with the boxes you want checked. Archie Mobile shows a line saying where on the computer to press it, since a phone cannot connect an account. Chat apps get the words only. It shows under a reply that names the Connections tab or an unconnected app. With no calendar connected, it also shows when you name your calendar app or the reply says none is connected. There is no button for a to-do list, since Todoist and Google Tasks are in different places. It opens the screen. Signing in is still yours to do. Chat apps get the words only.

entries.t: Connect an app's address for AI assistants
entries.s: Some apps hand out an address for AI assistants. Add it under Something else, and the tools that app offers join your agent's tools without an Archie update.
entries.x: On the Connections tab, under Apps, press Something else at the foot of the list. On the Connections tab, open Apps and press Something else. Under What do you call it?, type the app's name. Under Its address, paste the address the app gave you for AI assistants, then paste its key. If the app has you sign in on its own site instead, Archie opens that sign-in in your browser. A tool the app marks as read only runs on its own. Anything else waits for your yes, like every other change. The app has to give you a key or a sign-in. An address that refuses a key cannot be connected. An app that changes its sign-in often may ask you to sign in again after Archie restarts. It has had very little testing with real apps so far.

entries.s: Google, Microsoft, Telegram, Discord, Slack, Matrix, Todoist, Fireflies, GoHighLevel, and any service you connect with your own key are reached directly from your computer.
entries.x: On the Connections tab, under Email, calendar, files; Apps; Home devices; and Computer control. Google Drive is per file: your agent sees only the Sheets and Docs you pick in Google's picker. What your agent reads from a connected service goes to your AI company, like anything else it reads. A service you connected yourself is yours. We make no claim about it working.

entries.s: Add Philips Hue, WiZ or LIFX lights from your own wifi, and your agent switches them over that wifi. The request never leaves your network.
entries.x: On the Connections tab, under Home devices, press Look for devices. On the Connections tab, open Home devices. Press Look for devices. For a Hue bridge, press the round button on top of the bridge when Archie asks. Press Add beside each light you want. To find a Hue bridge, Archie asks Philips once which bridges have reported in from your network. Switching a light stays on your network. What your agent learns from a light, like its name and whether it is on, goes to your AI company like anything else it reads. No locks, thermostats or cameras. The Hue bridge talks to Philips on its own, and Archie has no part in that traffic.

entries.s: Connect iCloud, Fastmail, Yahoo, AOL, Zoho or GMX mail with an app password you make on the provider's own site, plus its calendar where it has one.
entries.x: On the Connections tab, under Email, calendar, files, choose iCloud or other email. On the Connections tab, open Email, calendar, files. Choose iCloud or other email, then your provider. Make an app password on the provider's site, paste it including spaces, and connect. There is no Sign in with Apple. The app password is the whole connection. The password is kept in your computer's password store and sent only to that provider's own mail and calendar servers. AOL and GMX have no calendar here. For the others, a calendar appears only if Archie found one while connecting. Your agent can do only what connecting proved, such as reading, sending, or the calendar.

entries.s: Once your Google account is connected, choosing which Drive files your agent may read is a separate step, and you can leave it for later.
entries.x: On the Connections tab, under Email, calendar, files. Choose files later shows while Google's file window is open, and Add files is on a Google account's row. Connect your Google account on the Connections tab, under Email, calendar, files. In the Google Drive window in your browser, choose files and press Select. Or press Choose files later, then press Add files on the account's row when you are ready. On a Mac only. Archie on Windows is still on 0.3.11, without it. Your agent can read only the Sheets and Docs you choose. Choose files later stops Archie waiting. It does not close the browser window or cancel Google's file window. Accounts are connected on the computer. Archie Mobile sends you there.

entries.s: Your agent thinks with an AI account you connect: Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, Groq, xAI, DeepSeek, or Mistral, or another service that works like OpenAI's.
entries.x: On each agent's Setup tab, under AI account. Keys you save are listed in Settings, under Saved keys. Open your agent's Setup tab and choose AI account. Pick an AI company. Paste the key you made on that company's website. The free credits you start with run on Claude, because that is the account we pay for. Changing it restarts your agent, which takes a few seconds. Archie does not promise that every AI company does every job equally well.

entries.t: Ask your agent to switch AI company
entries.s: Ask your agent to use a different AI company, such as "use ChatGPT instead", and it switches, or says where to paste a key if you have none saved.
entries.x: In a chat, ask your agent to use a different AI company. If it has no key for that company, paste one where it tells you. You can ask from Archie Mobile or a chat app, since it is a request in a conversation. It changes only when you ask in a conversation. A routine cannot switch it. The switch restarts your agent, which takes a few seconds. You can turn it off on the agent's Setup tab, under What it can do, with Change which AI answers.

entries.t: A model on your own computer
entries.s: Archie can run your agent on a model on your computer through Ollama, LM Studio or llama.cpp, after checking that the model can use a tool.
entries.x: On the agent's Setup tab, under AI account, in the Another provider panel. Install Ollama, LM Studio or llama.cpp and download a model. Open your agent's Setup tab, choose AI account, then Another provider. Pick the model Archie found and let Archie check it. Nothing is saved until the model has been handed a tool and used it, and many small models never do. Only where what you type goes changes. Your mail, your calendar, the pages your agent reads, and Archie's update and plan checks still use the internet. It is not the default and not the trial. Archie makes no promise about speed or quality on a model like this.

entries.s: Archie keeps its own estimate of what your agents' AI use has cost, this month and all time, by agent and by AI company.
entries.x: On the Account page, under Spending. Open the Account page and choose Spending. Pick This month or All time. It is an estimate from a price table inside Archie. The exact bill is on your AI company's own billing page. Some AI companies are not in the price table, and the page names them.

entries.t: A monthly limit on AI spending
entries.s: You can set one monthly limit on what your agents spend on thinking, all of them together. When the month reaches it, routines and reading new mail and texts pause until the first. Your agent still answers when you ask, and reminders still go off.
entries.x: On the Account page, under Spending: Monthly limit. Open the Account page and choose Spending. Switch on Monthly limit. Type an amount in whole dollars under Limit for one month, then press Save. Your own conversation keeps going past the limit, so a month can end above the number. The figure is an estimate, and the exact one is on your AI company's own billing page. A custom AI address you typed in yourself is not counted. It is off until you switch it on. It limits what your agents spend on thinking. Buying on a website has its own switch and limits, on the Connections tab under Computer control.

entries.t: Response quality, and Use this for every skill
entries.s: Pick Economy, Balanced or Best for your agent's replies, and tick Use this for every skill so its add-ons use that setting too.
entries.x: On the agent's Setup tab, under Response quality. Open your agent's Setup tab and choose Response quality. Pick Economy, Balanced or Best. Tick Use this for every skill to make every add-on follow it. Archie Mobile can change an agent's Response quality too, under Response quality in More. Many add-ons pick their own setting, so the setting alone barely changes the bill until the box is ticked. Ticking the box also moves add-ons off the level they chose, and Economy answers were weaker in our tests. Web searches stay on Balanced even with the box ticked.

entries.s: Pick your own model for any of Economy, Balanced and Best from your AI company's list, and it runs in replies, skills and anything on a schedule.
entries.x: On the agent's Setup tab, under Response quality, in Choose the models yourself. Open your agent's Setup tab and choose Response quality. Open Choose the models yourself. Pick a model for any setting, or press Put all three back to Archie's choices. Archie Mobile can do the same, under Response quality in More. It needs an AI account of your own. On the free credits or the plan with the AI included there is one model. Another provider runs the one model typed on its card, so there is nothing to pick there. Some AI companies publish no list, so you type the model's name from their website. A model you pick runs without extended thinking unless it is the one Archie would have used.

entries.s: Connect any AI service that works like OpenAI's, such as Venice, by pasting its address, a model name and a key.
entries.x: On the agent's Setup tab, under AI account, on the Another provider tile. Open your agent's Setup tab and choose AI account. Pick Another provider. Paste the service's address, a model name and a key, copied from its own website. Venice and services like it are not among the seven named AI companies. Archie says nothing about what that service does with what it receives. Read its own pages for that. It runs the one model you typed, whatever Response quality says.

entries.s: When the free credits or your plan's AI for the month run out, your agent says so once, with the ways to keep going, and keeps what you send.
entries.x: A card under the reply in your agent's chat, with Set up an AI account, See the plans, or Open the Account page, and Lists and Calendar. Press the way you want on the card. Keep typing if you like. Each message is kept, and your agent answers it once the AI is back. Archie Mobile shows the same ways, each saying where on the computer to do it, with Lists and Calendar to press. A chat app gets them in words. Only your own messages are kept: the newest 20, each cut at 600 characters, and a photo only as its caption. It picks up within about half an hour of the AI coming back, and only while Archie is open on your computer. A reminder asked for while the AI is out is set only once the AI is back, so it can be late. A chat app gets the ways in words, with no prices and no card.

entries.s: If the AI company has a passing problem, Archie asks it once more. If that fails too, the reply says whether anything was saved or sent, with Try again.
entries.x: Under the reply in your agent's chat. Press Try again to send the same words again. Archie Mobile, Telegram, Slack, and Discord show Try again under the reply. It asks once more, and a second failure reaches you. There is no Try again for a picture, a pin, a message over 2,000 characters, or a turn that already saved something. No button on Signal, iMessage, or Matrix, or in Archie while one of those is the chat app. When the AI runs out, you get the card of ways to keep going instead.

entries.t: Working numbers out in Python on a Mac
entries.s: When an answer has to be exactly right, like a total, a loan payment or a spreadsheet's figures, your agent can work it out in a short Python program instead of in its head, and shows you the program under its answer.
entries.x: In your chat with your agent: How I worked it out, under an answer worked out this way. Ask something whose answer has to be exactly right, or give your agent a spreadsheet and ask about its numbers. Press How I worked it out under the answer to see the program. On an iPhone, Archie Mobile shows How I worked it out too, with the first 1,200 characters of a long program. The program runs on the computer. On a Mac only. Archie on Windows is still on 0.3.11, without it. The program runs inside Archie with no internet, and it sees only copies of files you gave it. Your files are never changed: a chart or a cleaned copy is a new file. It has the usual tools for numbers, tables and charts, and nothing more can be added. The program can still be wrong, which is why it is shown. Someone else you let message your agent, or a teammate, has it only on Everything you can. Python is a one-time download of about 23 MB that Archie fetches on its own. Until it is here, your agent answers another way and says the answer was not worked out exactly. A chat app like Telegram gets the answer without the program.

entries.t: Choose what your agent can do
entries.s: Switches decide what your agent offers, such as setting reminders or reading the web; turn one off and each message costs a little less.
entries.x: On the agent's Setup tab, under What it can do, in Jobs it does for you and Changes it can make to itself. Open your agent's Setup tab and choose What it can do. Turn off any switch you do not want. Turning a switch off does not remove an add-on. Remove add-ons on the Skills tab. Each row says where the job still gets done with the switch off. Ask for something that is switched off and your agent names the screen that turns it back on. The saving is small and has not been measured.

entries.t: What your agent will never do
entries.s: Your agent is awake only when you write, a routine's time comes, or it checks a mailbox you connected. It cannot run a command or text anyone.
entries.x: The guide What your agent will never do, linked from the first screen of the first run. Archie Mobile shows the Python program under an answer, as Archie does. A chat app gets the answer without it. Each limit is on what it does. None of them makes the AI right, and a wrong draft you send is the realistic harm. It can still search the web, read pages and, with Computer control on, use a browser. Specialists you install can take a job from your agent, but cannot hand it on or start anything themselves. On a Mac its only code is a short Python program it runs inside Archie with no internet. Archie on Windows does not run it yet.

entries.s: If you tell your agent you are thinking about hurting yourself, or someone is putting you in danger, it steps out of character and names where to get help.
entries.x: It applies wherever you talk to your agent, including Archie Mobile and chat apps. In the US it names 988, to call or text. Elsewhere it names your local crisis line, your emergency number, or your doctor. Nobody at Otian AI sees the conversation, and nothing is reported. It is a language model reading text, so it can miss someone who does not say it plainly. It offers no counseling. It stops, says it cannot be the one to help, and names who can.

entries.s: On your own AI account, what you write goes straight from your computer to that AI company, and Otian is not in the middle and keeps no copy.
entries.x: Messages through a chat app such as Telegram cross that company's servers, and messages to Archie Mobile cross ours, locked so we cannot open them. The free credits you start with, and the plan with the AI included, run on our AI account, so while you use them your messages pass through our server on the way to Anthropic. Your AI company still receives what you write, and a web search runs on that company's own search service. Archie still checks your plan and counts add-on installs with our server. Neither carries your conversations. It does not make Archie HIPAA or GDPR compliant, because what you write still goes to a cloud AI company.

entries.t: No analytics, and crash reports you can turn off
entries.s: Archie has no analytics service, and its version check-in and its crash and error reports carry your account ID but never anything you wrote, received, or asked for.
entries.x: In Settings, under Privacy, the Send crash reports switch, with a list of what it sends. Open Settings and choose Privacy. Turn off Send crash reports. Archie Mobile has no analytics, crash reporting or advertising code in it. It is on until you turn it off. Off sends nothing more and deletes anything waiting to be sent. Reports carry your account ID, so they are not anonymous. An error that keeps happening sends its error line, and for an add-on, its name and the tool that failed. Your answer to How did you hear about Archie? is sent only when you press one, and this switch does not cover it.

entries.s: Archie checks for updates with a plain request that carries no version number, nothing identifying your computer, and no account.
entries.x: In Settings, under Updates. GitHub and Cloudflare, which serve the update file, see your computer's internet address and the time of the check.

entries.s: The keys you save for AI companies and services are kept in your computer's built-in password store, where we have no way to read them.
entries.x: In Settings, under Saved keys. A key pasted in Archie Mobile on iPhone travels to your computer locked so we cannot open it, and is stored there the same way. A key goes to its own company with each request, which is how that company knows it is you. While your agent is using a key, Archie holds it in memory.

entries.s: Archie writes down each time a saved key is used and each change to who or what can reach your agents, and shows if any line was changed.
entries.x: In Settings, under Privacy, in Access record. Open Settings and choose Privacy. Read Access record. Checked: nothing edited or removed means the check passed. It holds those actions only. What your agent read, wrote or sent is not in it. It shows a change after the fact. Someone who deletes the record and its note in the password store together leaves nothing to check. It stays on your computer, so we never see it and cannot vouch for it. Only Archie for Teams can export the whole record, with Export the whole record.

entries.t: No list of the add-ons you install
entries.s: Adding an add-on raises its public popularity count by one, and we keep only the running total, never a list of which add-ons are yours.
entries.x: The count request is signed in as you, so it is not anonymous. It is sent whichever AI account you use, and stops only if you block our server. Since we keep no list, a new computer needs your add-ons added again, unless you restore a backup.

entries.t: What Archie Mobile asks for on your phone
entries.s: Archie Mobile uses the camera, your photos, your files and the microphone only when you press to scan, pick, take or record something.
entries.x: This is about Archie Mobile itself, on iPhone and Android. A photo, video, file or recording goes to the computer running Archie, locked so we cannot open it, and your agent shows it to its AI company when it looks. On the talk screen, the microphone listens between turns until you press Done, and stops if you leave the app. Archie Mobile has no analytics or advertising code.

entries.s: Reset Archie erases your agents and your saved keys from your computer, disconnects every phone, and empties the phone mailbox.
entries.x: On the Account page, under Resetting Archie, press Reset Archie. On the Account page, choose Resetting Archie. Press Reset Archie, type reset, and press Erase and restart. It leaves the helper that wakes the computer for routines, and Open Archie at login stays as it was set. Downloaded voice and speech models stay, and so does a choice to turn off error reports. On Windows, the uninstaller's box Also remove my Archie data, agents, and settings is a different thing: it leaves your saved keys behind.

entries.t: How long the phone mailbox keeps things
entries.s: Messages between Archie Mobile and your computer wait in a mailbox on Otian's server. The phone deletes each once read, and your computer clears leftovers a day later.
entries.x: To empty it now, on your agent's Setup tab, under Chat app, press Archie Mobile, then Disconnect every phone. This is how Archie Mobile reaches the computer running Archie. There is no fixed limit in days. The clearing needs your computer on and Archie running. The picture of your agent the phone shows stays until you press Disconnect every phone, reset Archie, or delete your account.

entries.s: Nothing on the network can reach Archie. Only three things listen, on your computer and only while in use: a sign-in, the Google Drive picker, and the Computer control browser.
entries.x: Archie's web tools refuse private and local network addresses. Three things can reach local addresses: lights added on your wifi, an AI model on your computer, and the Computer control browser, which is off until you turn it on. The Computer control browser is fenced only by your Blocked sites list.

entries.t: An address your agent came up with waits for your yes
entries.s: Your agent opens a web page on its own only when the address came from you, from a page it already opened, or from a site you named in your message. An address it came up with itself, it shows you first and waits for your yes.
entries.x: In your chat with your agent, on a card with Open it and Don't open it. A search it wants to hand on asks with Go ahead and Don't. Press Open it, or Don't open it. When your agent asks before handing a search on, press Go ahead, or Don't. After your agent reads an email, a page or a file in a job, it asks before handing a search on, and a site you named waits for your yes too. Asking first has a cost: a page your agent wants to open on its own judgment waits for you. For about ten messages after it reads new mail or texts for you, so does a search it hands on or a site you name in passing. A skill that searches the web is given only the task: none of your memory, your profile, your files or the rest of the chat. A skill that searches the web reads only the one message it is handed, so name the subject when you follow up. Some questions about your own work still go to it, and it answers those without your lists. It does not stop everything. An instruction hidden in an email or a page can still add to your lists or save a note to your agent's memory, and that note can steer a later job. Two ways out remain. Text typed into a page already open goes wherever that page sends it, and a service you connected through its address for AI assistants can open pages on its own. A search still sends its words to your AI company's search service. Your agent judges whether your reply was a yes. Archie makes sure it comes in a later message from you. A routine running on its own is refused instead of asking.

entries.t: The plan with the AI included
entries.s: For $59 a month or $599 a year, Archie comes with $25 of Claude usage each month, so you need no AI account of your own.
entries.x: Offered when you choose a plan in Archie, beside the plan where you connect your own AI account. Choose a plan in Archie. Pick the one with the AI included. Your agent will not read your email or your texts on this plan. Both work once you connect an AI account of your own. The $25 refills each paid month and nothing rolls over. When it is used, your agent pauses until next month or until you connect your own AI account. What you write passes through our server on the way to Anthropic. The server records what each request cost, never what it said, and keeps no copy. Free credits you have left end when the plan starts.

entries.t: A 14-day trial on your own AI account
entries.s: When a computer has used its free credits, you can still try Archie for 14 days by connecting an AI account of your own.
entries.x: Archie offers it when the free credits cannot be claimed on your computer. Connect an AI account of your own when Archie offers the 14 days. Archie checks that the key works, then starts the trial. You pay your AI company for what your agent uses during the 14 days. Archie still checks your plan, checks for updates and reads the add-on store during the trial. Your conversations do not pass through us. It is offered only after the free credits are used up on that computer.

entries.s: During a free trial, a strip at the bottom of the window says what Archie costs afterward, and the Account page's Your plan row says the same.
entries.x: The strip at the bottom of the Archie window during a trial, with Get a plan. On the Account page, under Sign-in, the Your plan row, with See plans. Press Get a plan on the strip, or See plans on the Your plan row, to open the plan chooser. The strip and the row never name the plan with the AI included. The chooser behind Get a plan and See plans does. Archie for Teams has no free tier. It is $99 a month or $999 a year, on an AI account of your own. The number of answers left on the free credits is an estimate, since one long document costs as much as many short questions. The free credits may be switched off, so the credits line may not appear.

entries.s: Ask your agent what Archie costs or the cheapest way to keep going, and Archie answers from its own price list without asking the AI.
entries.x: In your agent's chat. Type a short question, such as "What does Archie cost?" Ask from Archie Mobile or a chat app, and the answer arrives like any reply. The question has to be about Archie, the AI, or your plan. "What do we charge for a unit?" goes to your agent as usual. Only your own typed question. A teammate's question goes to the agent. Asked how much is left, it says the count and the day, never a price. At about three answers left on the free credits, one line under a reply says so, once until the balance goes up.

entries.t: Add your AI account after buying a plan
entries.s: Buy a plan without the AI in it, and Archie asks for your AI account next, so your first agent starts as soon as it is made.
entries.x: The Add your AI account screen, right after you buy a plan and before Archie opens. Later, it is Settings at the bottom of the left sidebar, then Saved keys. Pick your AI company, or press Show me how for the steps to get a key. Paste the key and press Save and open Archie. Or press Not now, and Archie asks again the next time it opens. It saves an AI account you already have. Show me how walks you through getting one from the AI company. Your agents cannot answer anybody until an AI account is saved. Archie for Teams never includes the AI. Archie Mobile has no checkout, so this happens on the computer only.

entries.t: Free on your own AI account, 20 jobs a day
entries.s: Paste a key from an AI company and Archie opens for free, with every skill and routine, up to 20 jobs a day. A plan takes the limit off.
entries.x: Paste the key when Archie first asks for one, or on your agent's Setup tab, under AI account. Make a key at an AI company such as Anthropic or OpenAI. Paste it into Archie when it asks, or on your agent's Setup tab, under AI account. Archie Mobile is not included; it needs a plan or a free trial that is still running. 20 jobs a day. A job is a reply to you, a routine running, or an email it reacts to, and the count starts again at midnight. Routines and the mail and text watches stop at 15, so the last 5 jobs of the day are yours. Free covers one agent, checked when you add one. A plan runs up to ten. Archie only. Archie for Teams has nothing free.

entries.t: Your plan follows your Otian account
entries.s: A plan lives on your Otian account, so signing in on another computer gets the same plan.
entries.x: Only the plan follows you. Your agents are files on the computer, and a backup file is how they move. Add-ons are added again on a new computer. The free starter credits are counted per computer and do not follow the account.

entries.t: What happens when a plan ends
entries.s: A plan you stop runs to the end of the period you paid for. Nothing on your computer is deleted, and what opens next depends on your edition and key.
entries.x: On the Account page, under Your plan, press Manage plan. Save a backup first, on the Account page, under Backups. On the Account page, under Your plan, press Manage plan to stop it. On Archie with an AI key saved, Archie keeps opening at 20 jobs a day. Without a saved key, it asks for one. Archie for Teams has nothing free, so it asks for a plan. Every agent you made stays and keeps working. Adding one past the free allowance of one agent is refused. Save a backup before you stop. The screen that asks for a plan also has Save a backup of your agents.

entries.t: Archie and Archie for Teams on one computer
entries.s: Archie for Teams installs beside Archie as its own app, with its own data and its own keys, so one computer can run both.
entries.x: Each is its own app on this computer: Archie, and Archie for Teams. Install Archie for Teams. Archie stays as it is, with its own agents. The two don't share agents, lists or connected accounts. To bring your agents across, save a backup in Archie and open it in Archie for Teams. Keys and sign-ins are kept apart too, so you connect your accounts in each one.

entries.t: Move your agents into Archie for Teams
entries.s: When you hire, save a backup in Archie and open it in Archie for Teams, and your agents arrive with their knowledge, lists, routines and memory.
entries.x: In Archie, on the Account page, under Backups. In Archie for Teams, the first run asks Have you used Archie before? with Open a backup. In Archie, open the Account page and choose Backups. Press Save a backup. In Archie for Teams, press Open a backup and pick the file. Reconnect your accounts from the list it shows. Keys and sign-ins do not come across, so you reconnect your accounts once, from a list. It goes one way only. Archie keeps its own copy of each agent, so press Stop on each one there. Opening it replaces the agents already in Archie for Teams, which are kept in a folder and can be put back.

entries.s: A new Archie for Teams agent starts with Team Starter: a shared to-do list, a record of who took which job, web lookups, and a personality naming who it answers.
entries.x: In the Marketplace, Team Starter holds Task Manager, Who's Got This, Researcher, and The Team Assistant. On the first run, Who is on my team? puts "On my team:" in the message box. Archie Mobile's store lists Team Starter when the paired computer runs Archie for Teams. It goes on a new agent without asking, the way Everyday Assistant does on Archie. Archie for Teams only. It is not in the store on Archie.

entries.t: Write down who each teammate is
entries.s: When you add someone, write down their name and what they do, and an email or phone number if you like. Your agent then knows who is on the team, so asked to write to Dana it already has her address.
entries.x: On the agent's Setup tab, under Who can message it. Add someone asks Who are you adding?, and each person's row has Edit. On the agent's Setup tab, under Who can message it, press Add someone. Under Who are you adding?, write their name and what they do, and an email or phone number if you like. Make their link or code, press Copy message, and send it to them yourself. To change what is written later, press Edit on their row. On an iPhone, Archie Mobile lists each person by name and what they do, under More, then Teammates. Your agent knows only what is written on the rows, and never searches your mail or contacts for anyone. Everyone on the agent sees names and what each person does. Your agent is told the emails and phone numbers on your messages, and on a teammate's messages only that teammate's own. Archie doesn't send the invite. You copy the message and send it however you like. Like everything your agent is told, what is written goes to your AI company.

entries.s: On a shared agent you choose what the people you let in can do: ask it things, also add to and change its lists, or everything you can. In the middle setting a teammate can log a delivery or add a task to the agent's lists, and still cannot send your mail, change your calendar, or use the apps you connected.
entries.x: On the agent's Setup tab, under Who can message it, in What teammates can do, once someone else is on the agent. On the agent's Setup tab, open Who can message it. Under What teammates can do, pick Talk to your agent, Talk and add to your lists, or Everything you can. On an iPhone, Archie Mobile has the same three answers under More, then Teammates. Talk to your agent is the default. A teammate's adds and changes to entries happen at once, with an undo, as yours do. Removing an entry waits for a yes in their own chat, from them. Making a new list or adding a column stays yours. On every setting, a teammate reads every list the agent can. On a list that says whose each entry is, their answers keep to their own work. A task in Todoist or Google Tasks is a connected app, so the middle setting leaves it out. A task in Task Manager is an entry on a list, so it is in. Nobody has picked it on a real agent yet.

entries.s: Everybody on an agent has a role. The owner is who the agent works for, and its routines report to them. An admin can change the agent and decide who is on it, the same as the owner, and whoever set it up can make the right person the owner.
entries.x: On the agent's Setup tab, under Who can message it: Role and Can on each person's row, and This computer is under the list. On the agent's Setup tab, open Who can message it. On a person's row, pick Teammate, Admin or Owner under Role. For a teammate, pick what they can do under Can. Picking Owner asks first, then hands the agent over. Under the list, pick who This computer is, so what they type there is from them and they see their own email there. On an iPhone, from Archie Mobile 1.4, the same choices are on a person under More, then Teammates. An admin gets the same page on their own phone, under Settings. The old owner stays on as an admin, so nobody loses access. Routines report to the new owner only after they send the agent a private message. Until then, reports land in Archie's own chat on the computer. A teammate can't make themselves an admin. Only an admin or the owner can. An admin never reads the owner's own mail. An account marked as somebody's stays theirs. Whoever sits at the computer can change people there, whatever their role, so a mistake can always be undone. Both people are told about a hand-over in their own chat when Archie has one on record for them. Otherwise they see it on the list. Nobody has used it on a real agent yet.

entries.t: Add and edit people from your phone
entries.s: In Archie Mobile, under More, then Teammates, you can add someone, edit their name and contact details, take them off, or stop a waiting invite. You copy or share the invite message from your phone.
entries.x: In Archie Mobile, under More, then Teammates. In Archie Mobile, open More, then Teammates. Press Add someone, or open a person to edit or remove them. Press Copy message or Share message, and send it to them however you like. On an iPhone, from Archie Mobile 1.3. The Android download does not have it yet, so adding people there happens at the computer. Only the owner's phone can, and an admin's own phone. A teammate who is not an admin can't. Archie doesn't send the invite. You choose where to paste or share the message. An invite makes nobody the owner, and it doesn't lift your plan's limit on people. The computer running Archie does the work, so it has to be awake, connected to the internet, and running Archie. Reset access stays at the computer.

entries.t: Teammates set and cancel reminders for themselves
entries.s: A teammate can ask your agent to remind them of something, and it reminds them in the chat they asked in, never on your to-do list. They can cancel their own reminders and nobody else's.
entries.x: In the chat with your agent. Your Calendar tab says whose each reminder is, such as "For Dana Miller, who set it", and so does Jobs. A teammate asks your agent, such as "Remind me at 3 to call Ellen." To remind a teammate yourself, name them, such as "Remind Todd at 3 to call Ellen." On an iPhone, Archie Mobile's Calendar says whose each reminder is. Everyone on the agent can read every reminder, and the list says whose each one is. A teammate's reminder arrives as a message in the chat they set it in, with no notification from Archie. You can cancel any reminder, and delete any on the Calendar. A reminder for someone who hasn't joined yet is held for them. Until they join and write to your agent, it comes to you. Your agent refuses a name nobody on the agent goes by, and offers to set it for you instead. To-dos stay on your list, and there is no giving one to a teammate.

entries.s: Your agent's Dashboard lists your team: what each person does, how many messages they sent the agent this week and how many jobs those started, and when they last wrote. Press a name to read what they said.
entries.x: On the agent's Dashboard, in Your team this week. Open your agent's Dashboard and find Your team this week. Press a name to read that person's conversation with your agent. Or ask your agent what your team has been doing, or what one of them asked today, and it tells you, with the time of each message. On an iPhone, from Archie Mobile 1.3, the Dashboard shows the same card with counts and times only. What anyone said is read on the computer. The card is on your computer and your phone, and teammates don't see it. This week means the last seven days. A message is any message a teammate sent your agent, a thank-you included, and one sent while this computer was asleep is not counted. A job is work their message started that changed something, as the Jobs tab lists it. Your agent quotes what teammates asked to you alone. A teammate asking hears only about their own jobs. On the phone the counts can be up to ten minutes behind.

entries.t: A teammate asking about the work gets their own entries
entries.s: When a teammate asks your agent about a list that says whose each entry is, they hear about their own entries and the ones with nobody named, and an entry they add is theirs. You still see every entry.
entries.x: On a list with a column named Agent, Assigned to, Assignee, Driver, Tech, Technician or Owner. To narrow one teammate further, use Sees under their role on the Setup tab, under Who can message it. Give the list a column that says whose each entry is, such as Assigned to. To have a teammate see only entries with their name, set Sees to Only rows with their name under their role. A teammate on Archie Mobile sees the same entries on their phone. On an iPhone, from Archie Mobile 1.4, you can set Sees for a person under More, then Teammates. This keeps a teammate's answers to their own work. Documents, shared files and what your agent remembers are not narrowed, and every teammate reads a list with no such column in full. In a group chat where several people speak at once, your agent can't tell whose turn it is and sees every entry. Names are matched as written, so "D. Miller" in the column names nobody on the team. An entry with your name on it is yours, so a teammate doesn't see it. You and admins see every entry, whatever Sees says. Only the real estate setup gets the column by itself: People, Deals and Listings come with an Agent column.

entries.t: What a teammate saved, told to you
entries.s: When someone on your team tells your agent something that adds to or changes one of your lists, you get a message saying what they saved. Under their reply, they see that you are told.
entries.x: In your own chat with the agent, on the computer and your phone. A teammate on Archie Mobile on an iPhone gets the same button to copy a text or open it in Messages, and the same card for entries Archie drafted, that you get. List saves only. Mail, drafts and calendar changes are not told, and neither are your own. It is a notice after the fact. Nothing waits for your yes. A teammate's card of drafted entries has no Undo. On a chat app a teammate gets no button, and Archie says so.

entries.s: Right-click an agent in Archie to open it, start or stop it, rename it, change how it looks, or delete it.
entries.x: On an agent in the sidebar's list of agents, on the agent you are in, or on its card on the Company page. Right-click an agent. Pick what to do. To delete it, type its name first. In Archie Mobile on iPhone, hold an agent's card on the Agents screen for the same menu, while the computer running Archie is on. A deleted agent cannot be brought back. Deleting an agent leaves its accounts and keys for your other agents.

entries.t: Keeps running with the window closed
entries.s: Close Archie's window and your agent keeps working. Archie stays running in the Dock on a Mac, or by the clock on Windows, until you quit it.
entries.x: On a Mac, click Archie in the Dock or its icon in the menu bar to bring the window back. On Windows, click its icon by the clock. Your agent runs only while Archie is running and your computer is awake. Quitting Archie switches it off. Quitting while an agent is running asks first.

entries.s: Archie opens by itself, with no window, when you sign in to your computer, so your agent is answering again after a restart.
entries.x: Settings, General, Open Archie at login. To turn it off, open Settings, then General, and switch off Open Archie at login. An update turned it on once for everyone, so check the switch if you had turned it off before. Once you switch it off, it stays off.

entries.t: Open Archie with a few keys
entries.s: By default, press Control, Shift and Space on a Mac, or Ctrl, Alt and Space on Windows, and Archie comes forward on your last chat, ready to type.
entries.x: Settings, General, Open Archie from any app. Press the keys in any app while Archie is running. To pick other keys, open Settings, then General, and press Change keys under Open Archie from any app. Switch it off on the same row if you don't want it. It works while Archie is running, including with the window closed, and not after you quit. Your computer tells Archie only when those keys are pressed, and nothing else you type. On a Mac, another app using the same keys may get them first. Nothing happens when you press them? on the row says what to do. It brings Archie's own window forward. There is no small floating box.

entries.t: Archie in the Mac menu bar
entries.s: On a Mac, Archie has an icon in the menu bar at the top of the screen that opens it or quits it.
entries.x: The Archie icon in the Mac menu bar, with Open Archie and Quit Archie. On Windows, the icon by the clock does the same. Click the icon in the menu bar. Choose Open Archie or Quit Archie. There is no switch to hide it. It is there whenever Archie runs on a Mac. Quit Archie asks first while an agent is running.

entries.t: Bring an agent over from OpenClaw
entries.s: Archie reads your OpenClaw agent's folder on this computer and shows you what it would make before it makes anything. Its personality, what it knows about you, its notes, its skills and its scheduled jobs become the new agent's.
entries.x: Press New agent in the sidebar, then Bring one over from OpenClaw under Where should it start? Press New agent in the sidebar, then Bring one over from OpenClaw. Press See what is in it, or Choose the folder if Archie did not find it. Read Here is what Archie will make, with what stays behind and why. Press the button at the bottom that makes the agent. Bringing it over sends nothing anywhere and changes nothing of OpenClaw's, and none of OpenClaw's keys or passwords come over. Notes and skills come over word for word, so anything you wrote into them comes too. A skill that needs a program stays behind, and so does a job that runs one or whose schedule a routine can't say exactly. OpenClaw's chat apps, tools and plugins stay behind too. Its newest notes go into memory and the rest into older memory, which your agent looks at only when what you say matches a note. entries.x: Your agent can read your Zoom calls, with no Zoom account and nothing to connect. When you record a Zoom meeting, Zoom saves it in a folder on this computer. Archie reads what is in that folder and writes up what was said, here, with nothing sent anywhere. Turn it on under Connections, then Apps, then Zoom. Only calls you host are saved that way, and only the ones you pressed Record on, unless you have turned on "Record automatically as I start a meeting" in Zoom. Zoom often writes the transcript itself, and when it has, that is what Archie reads: it says who said which line, it takes no time, and it uses none of this computer's power. A call with no transcript beside it is transcribed here instead, and then the write-up says what was discussed and who was on the call but never who said what, because the audio does not carry that. Meeting Notes reads whichever meeting source you have, and any one of them is enough. A recording on this computer, a Fireflies key, or both. The card that asks for one no longer reads as though Fireflies were the only answer. Your agent tells you what it is costing you. A week after you start it says what it has spent so far and what that works out to over a month, then once a month after that. It says nothing at all rather than guess when it cannot put a price on something. Ask about your week and it reads every calendar you have connected, not just the first one. entries.x: Archie now comes with the AI included, if you want it that way. $59 a month or $599 a year buys the same plan plus $25 of Claude usage every month, so there is no AI account to open and no second bill. Tick "With the AI included" when you pick a plan. Your agent runs on our Anthropic account, which means what you write to it passes through our server on the way to Anthropic; nothing there writes it down, we keep no copy, and we use none of it. Email is the one thing this plan does not do: your agent will not read or write mail while it is thinking on our account, because the people who write to you never agreed to that. Connect an AI account of your own and every email feature starts working, with nothing to switch. When the $25 is used, your agent pauses until next month. On that plan, and on the free credits, the Response quality control on an agent's page now says that it changes nothing until you connect an AI account of your own, instead of looking like a setting that does something. Any service that publishes an MCP server can be connected now. GitHub, Linear, Stripe and Cloudflare are on the Connections tab under MCP servers, and "Another MCP server" takes any address you have. Paste the key, Archie asks the server what it can do, and your agent can use every tool the server offers: the read-only ones on the spot, and anything that changes something only after you approve it, the same way a web request works today. Ten more services have an add-on that knows how to use them: Airtable, Calendly, GitLab, Lunch Money, Mercury, Readwise, Stripe, Splitwise, YNAB and Zotero. Each one was written from that service's own documentation, so your agent is told the real endpoints instead of guessing. A key you paste for a service no add-on uses works anyway. The Routines card names the sleep and opens a list of steps for keeping this computer awake, instead of sending you to look at Archie, where nothing is wrong. Pick the provider on the Connections tab, make an app password on that provider's own website (Archie links you straight to the page), and paste it once. iCloud, Fastmail, Yahoo and Zoho bring their calendar with them. Everything already true of Gmail is true here: a reply goes out only when you send it or set a time, and mail it files is moved to Archive rather than deleted. Newsletters and mailing lists stop being read by the AI. Archie used to skip them using Gmail's own Promotions and Social labels, which no other provider has, so an Outlook or iCloud mailbox was paying to have every newsletter read. It now recognizes bulk mail from the message itself, on every provider. A receipt from a shop is not bulk and still reaches you. Tell your agent what you wish it could do, and it writes the skill. Say it in your own words in chat, and it comes back with a card: the name, what would set it off, and which of your accounts it would use. Nothing is added until you press Keep it. Every add-on is included with Archie. The Buy button, the prices on the cards, and the block that used to sit in front of Meeting Notes are all gone, because there was never anything to pay for. Archie can keep a backup for you, once a week, on its own. Choose a folder once and it writes one every week and keeps the last three. Restore it on the same machine after a mishap and nothing is disturbed. Saving a backup asks whether to stop the agents on this computer. That is the moment somebody moving to a new machine is standing in front of the old one, and two computers answering the same mailbox is the thing nobody notices until both have replied. entries.x: Your agent can now do a job on a website end to end: sign in where you sign in, click through, download what it came for, hand it to you, and keep it. Most of this release is that one job, found by collecting a real bank statement over and over until there was nothing left to go wrong. The browser window opens on your Mac's own chip. It was launching the Intel build through Rosetta, which is the whole reason the window it opened felt slow. The Websites panel says whether each site is signed in, and when it last was. It said nothing, so a site that had signed you out looked exactly like one that had not. Closing the sign-in window is noticed. The panel used to keep saying the window was open, because it watched for the program rather than for a page, and closing the last window does not close Chrome. "A window just opened" is now said when a window has opened, rather than when the program was still starting. Your agent stops reloading over your sign-in. Asked to open a site it was already looking at, it went back to the front page, which on a bank signs you straight back out. A file a site hands over lands where the job can find it, and the job waits for it to arrive. It was being told where to put downloads one tab at a time, so four or five statements went to a folder nobody looked in, and a file still arriving when the browser closed was reported as one that never started. The same file handed over twice arrives once. "I'll do this bit" ends with a button. You had to type "done" at an agent that had just given you buttons for everything else. Your agent can read back the question it asked you. It sends a question as the caption on a picture of the screen, and could not see that caption afterwards, so your answer meant nothing to it and the job went round in circles. It stops handing you the clicking. Asked to sign in, it now names the window already open in front of you, instead of a screen inside Archie that does not exist. A browser job gets the room to finish. Every job stopped after ten steps, and for a browser a step is a click: one bank statement spent all ten opening the site, clicking through, downloading the PDF, sending it to its owner and filing the record, and then said "Reached the tool call limit" underneath the statement it had just collected. Everything below is what that found. Eighty eight problems, all of them closed, and then a second pass by readers who had not been told what was fixed. Your agent knows it is shared. On an agent with more than one person on it, it was never told that, so "can Sam see this?" and "who else reads these?" were answered from a guess. It now knows who the owner is, who is speaking, and that the owner can read the conversation, and it says so when somebody asks. Everything your agent sends without being asked now goes to a chat you picked. Routine reports, reminders, watcher cards and morning briefings all went to whichever conversation happened to speak to it first, which on a shared agent could be a colleague's. Approving somebody from the waiting list now sends them a message. They were let in silently, so the first thing a new person heard from your agent was the answer to something they had asked before they were let in, and nobody ever told them the owner can read what they write. You can ask your agent whether a routine actually ran. "Did my morning brief go out?" and "has the pipeline report ever worked?" now have a real answer, including "it has never run", which is usually a computer that was asleep at the scheduled minute rather than anything broken. Switching a routine off by asking now switches it off. It reported success and kept firing until Archie was restarted. Removing a skill now takes its routines off the clock with it. They kept their schedule, fired every morning doing nothing, and stamped themselves as having run. A routine you add by asking for it keeps your time zone. It was set in UTC, so "every weekday at 7" meant 2am for somebody in Chicago, and the confirmation never named the hour. A routine whose time passed while the computer was asleep is delivered late instead of thrown away, and a routine that is broken says so on the second failure rather than after two more weeks of its schedule. You can talk to your agent in the Archie window and be answered out loud. A voice note recorded there came back as a paragraph to read, while the same voice note sent from a chat app was answered in speech. A spoken "go ahead" now lands on the card you aimed it at. entries.x: Your email signature belongs to an address now, not to the whole agent. On an agent your team shares, a reply written from a colleague's own address went out over the owner's name, and the one person who could see that happening was the client reading it. Every address is signed with its own signature. An address that has none is signed with the name of whoever it belongs to. A signature can be a picture. Put a logo beside the words, or use an image that is the whole signature with the name, title and phone drawn into it. You pick small, medium or large, and the preview is drawn at the size that goes out rather than as a thumbnail, so you find out it is too big before a client does. Somebody who is not the owner can set their own signature by telling the agent in chat. The Archie window belongs to the owner, so until now the owner was typing everybody's signature. A draft can wait for a time you pick. Every draft your agent hands you has a Send later button offering an hour from now, three hours, or the next morning, each printed as the time it actually comes to. If the other person writes back on that thread before it goes, the queued reply stops itself and hands the draft back to you with a line at the top saying why. Nothing leaves your account unless you send it or set the time for it yourself. Your agent can start an email, not only answer one. "Send Sam an email saying let's get lunch" used to come back as an explanation of why it could only reply to mail already in your inbox. Campaign Watch is new. It reads your lemlist campaigns and tells you who wrote back, what they said, and which campaign has quietly stopped working. It writes the replies and you send them. On a shared agent, somebody who is not the owner can answer mail sent to their own address. Every mail action counted as acting on the owner's accounts, so the only way to let a colleague reply to their own client was to hand them the owner's mailbox as well. A calendar can now be shared while the mail on the same account stays private. Sharing somebody's working hours, which is what colleagues need from each other all day, used to mean sharing their inbox too. Connected apps say whose they are: one person's, or the whole business's. There was one key per service, so "add that to my list" meant the owner's list wherever the person asking sat. Meeting notes accounts are one per person as well.

An expired sign-in, a permission a workplace withdrew, or Outlook having a bad minute all used to arrive looking identical to a quiet morning: "the inbox is empty". Answering in words still works: say "did that" or "move it to four" and the buttons settle themselves. Ask to be reminded and you get a reminder. It used to write a task instead, which is a row you have to go and look at and interrupts nobody. entries.x: Your new agent asks what your days look like, then sets itself up from the answers. The skills and routines that fit your work are chosen and switched on while you are still talking to it, and it tells you what it added. Its page opens on what arrived: each ability named, with what it does, and how to take any of them back off. You can tell your agent to remove a skill or pause a routine and it does it, after one tap to confirm. Pausing keeps the routine and everything you set on it. Waiting On follows up across texts as well as email. Ask by email, get the answer as a text, and it still closes the loop. On a Mac, with the text watch on. Archie for Business asks about the business: what it does, who its customers are, and who else will be talking to it. It no longer asks a company owner their age. Your agent answers on iMessage, on a Mac. That makes six chat apps, alongside Telegram, Discord, Slack, Signal and Matrix. You can talk to your agent in Archie's own window. It is one conversation, so a question you start in your chat app can be finished here. Send it a photo and it looks at the photo. It can make pictures too. Send a voice note instead of typing, and have replies read out loud. Your agent can use a website itself, the same way you would, when there is no direct connection to it. Outlook and Microsoft calendars work the way Google's do. Sign in once and your agent can read the mail and the diary. "Remind me to pay the water bill tomorrow at 10am" now sets a reminder. Your agent can learn how you write from what you have already sent, and draft in your voice. The store has shelves, packs and a cart, so a set of add-ons installs in one go. Archie has a face. Ember is the app's own character, and every agent gets its own version of him. Dark mode is stone rather than brown, and every color in the app was measured against its background so nothing is left faint. On Windows: the media tools (transcription, video) install on Windows now, and this is the first version Windows can update itself from. Fixed: sixteen routines woke up every morning to work out whether it was their day. They run on the day they mean now. Fixed: a restart could overwrite your agent's first message, and a long reply stopped one message short of the bottom of the window.

Archie updates itself. When a new version is ready, a banner appears in the app; one click downloads it, verifies it, and restarts. A much smaller download. Media tools (video, transcription) now download only when you install a skill that needs them, instead of shipping inside every copy. Bug fixes and stability improvements across sign-in and the marketplace.
